questions.text: Which designation was created to run the Indian administration after the Revolt of 1857 ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. The Government of India Act 1858 abolished Company rule and put a Secretary of State for India in the British cabinet to supervise Indian administration through a Council of India — that post was the new apex of control after 1857. Lieutenant Governors and Chief Commissioners already existed at provincial level; External Affairs Minister is a modern title.

questions.text:
Match the following :
a. Dinabandhu Mitra - I. Satyagraha of Bardoli
b. Baba Ramchandra - II. Satyagraha of Mulshi
c. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel - III. Struggle of Ayodhya farmers
d. Senapati Bapat - IV. The Drama of 'Nil Darpan'
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Dinabandhu Mitra wrote the drama 'Nil Darpan' (a–IV); Baba Ramchandra led the Ayodhya farmers' struggle in Awadh (b–III); Sardar Patel headed the Bardoli Satyagraha (c–I); Senapati Bapat was central to the Mulshi Satyagraha (d–II). Swapping Patel and Bapat's satyagrahas is the usual trap.

questions.text:
Which statements are correct regarding the 'Indian Association'?
a. Dadabhai Naoroji took the initiative for the establishment of the Association.
b. Objective was to create friendly relationship between the Hindus and the Muslims.
c. Pherozeshah Mehta and K.T. Telang ran the Association.
d. Efforts were made to enhance the age for Civil Services Examination.

options.A: a and b statements are correct
options.B: a, b and c statements are correct
options.C: b and c statements are correct
options.D: b and d statements are correct

questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. The Indian Association (1876) was launched by Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose, not Dadabhai Naoroji — so statement (a) is incorrect. It did aim at Hindu–Muslim goodwill (b) and campaigned to raise the age limit for the ICS exam (d). Pherozeshah Mehta and K.T. Telang belong to Bombay Presidency politics, not this body — statement (c) is incorrect.

questions.text: For which session of the Congress did the British officers try not giving any venue for it ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. For the 1888 Allahabad session the British administration tried to deny a venue, forcing the Congress to hold it at the Rasulabad garden instead. Mumbai (1889), Madras (1887), and Calcutta (1886) sessions did not face that particular obstruction.

questions.text:
What are the salient features of the Civil Disobedience Movement ?
a. Participation of the Pathans under the leadership of Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan.
b. Mahatma Gandhi returned the award of 'Kaisar-i-Hind' to the Government.
c. Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Salt Satyagraha.
d. Best Performance of Women.

options.A: a and c statements are correct
options.B: b, c and d statements are correct
options.C: a, c and d statements are correct
options.D: b and d statements are correct

questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan's Khudai Khidmatgar brought Pathans into the Civil Disobedience Movement (a); Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Salt Satyagraha after Gandhi's arrest (c); and women's participation was unusually strong (d). Statement (b) is wrong — Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in 1920 during the Non-Cooperation phase, not CDM.

questions.text: Devidas Kamble was the leader of the _______ from Pathri in Marathwada.
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Devidas Kamble was a Matang Samaj leader from Pathri in Marathwada who worked for the rights and organisation of the Matang community in the early twentieth century. Mahar, Mathadi, and Malkari samajs had different social bases and leaders.

questions.text: Khaksar means the
questions.explanation: Pick option A. The Khaksars were a militant Muslim organisation founded by Allama Mashriqi in the 1930s, known for their uniformed drills and paramilitary discipline. It was not a Hindu, Sikh, or Gurkha body.

questions.text: Who from the following persons were participants in the establishment of 'Hindustani Lal Sena' in Vidarbha ?

options.A: Madan Lal Bagdi, Vinayak S. Dandekar and Shyam Narayan Kashmiri
options.C: Rajguru, Sukhdeo and Shyam Narayan Kashmiri

questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Hindustani Lal Sena in Vidarbha was set up with Madan Lal Bagdi, Vinayak S. Dandekar, and Shyam Narayan Kashmiri among its founders — a regional revolutionary network, not the Lahore conspiracy trio of Rajguru and Sukhdev alone.

questions.text: Moreshwar Vasudeo Abhyankar was a Home Rule activist from
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Moreshwar Vasudeo Abhyankar was a Home Rule League activist from the Vidarbha region who worked to spread Tilak's and Besant's Home Rule message in Central India. He was not primarily associated with Marathwada, Konkan, or Khandesh.

questions.text: Dalhousie's policies of Imperialism, Subsidiary Alliance System and Doctrine of Lapse were the ________ causes of the Revolt of 1857.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Dalhousie's annexations, Subsidiary Alliance, and Doctrine of Lapse stripped princes of power and territory — that is a political grievance driving the 1857 revolt. Social, economic, and military causes are real too, but these three policies are textbook political triggers.

questions.text:
Khadilkar started 'Navakal' newspaper in 1925. Besides politics, which other subjects from the following were dealt in it ?
a. Trade
b. Education
c. Market Price
d. Cinema
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Khadilkar's 'Navakal' (1925) carried political news alongside trade reporting and market-price columns that ordinary readers tracked daily. Education and cinema were not its highlighted non-political beats in the sources this paper follows.

questions.text:
Which of the following small scale industries was not incorporated in the 'Wardha Scheme of Education' of Gandhiji ?
a. Agriculture
b. Shoemaking
c. Pottery
d. Woodwork
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to option A before MPSC withdrew the item; Gandhi's Wardha Scheme of Education normally lists agriculture, pottery, and woodwork among basic crafts, so the 'NOT incorporated' stem clashes with standard Nai Talim lists.

questions.text:
Match the following :
a. Rast Goftar - I. Tatya Chhatre
b. Dnyan Sindhu - II. Krishnaji Trimbak Ranade
c. Dnyan Prakash - III. Vishwanath Narayan Mandalik
d. Native Opinion - IV. Dadabhai Naoroji
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Rast Goftar was Dadabhai Naoroji's paper (a–IV); Dnyan Sindhu was linked to Tatya Chhatre (b–I); Dnyan Prakash to Krishnaji Trimbak Ranade (c–II); Native Opinion to Vishwanath Narayan Mandalik (d–III). Mixing Mandalik and Naoroji on the same weekly is the common distractor.

questions.text: Who among the following was involved in the Mulshi Satyagraha along with Pandurang Bapat ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Tatyasaheb Karandikar worked alongside Senapati Pandurang Bapat in the Mulshi Satyagraha against the Tata hydro project. Bhalekar, Jawalkar, and Shinde were active in other peasant or labour movements, not this Poona-area satyagraha pair.

questions.text: Who established the 'Rashtriya Mill Majdoor Sangh' (RMMS) in Mumbai ?
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to option A (G.D. Ambedkar) before MPSC withdrew the item; most labour histories credit N.M. Joshi with founding the Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh in Mumbai in 1925, so the stem allows more than one defensible name.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is responsible for blowing of monsoon winds in India?

options.B: Sea on three sides of India
options.C: Existence of jet stream between 30° to 40° latitude belt

questions.explanation: Go with option D. India's summer monsoon needs the vast heating of the subcontinental landmass, the sea on three sides shaping onshore flow, and the subtropical jet stream near 30°–40°N steering the system — all three factors work together, not one alone.

questions.text: Arrange the correct sequence of cement industry from North to South.

options.A: Chittorgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Khetri, Dalmia Dadri
options.B: Dalmia Dadri, Sawai Madhopur, Chittorgarh, Khetri
options.C: Sawai Madhopur, Chittorgarh, Khetri, Dalmia Dadri
options.D: Dalmia Dadri, Khetri, Sawai Madhopur, Chittorgarh

questions.explanation: Pick option D. From north to south the cement centres run Dalmia Dadri (Haryana belt), Khetri (Rajasthan), Sawai Madhopur (Rajasthan), then Chittorgarh (southern Rajasthan) — latitude drops as you move down that list.

questions.text: In which State is Noonmati oil refinery located?
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Noonmati oil refinery sits near Guwahati in Assam, processing crude from the Assam oil fields. It is not in Bihar or Gujarat; 'None of the above' is incorrect because Assam is correct.

questions.text: Kattha is obtained from ______ tree.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Kattha (catechu) is extracted from the heartwood of the khair (Acacia catechu) tree and is used in paan, dyeing, and tanning. Sundri, teak, and generic acacia are not the standard source named in geography texts.

questions.text: _______ State is leading in wind power energy.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Tamil Nadu has long led India in installed wind-power capacity thanks to the strong wind corridor along its coast and Ghats — ahead of Maharashtra, Kerala, and Karnataka in the 2018-era rankings this paper expects.

questions.text: _______ is the headquarters of North-Eastern Railway Zone.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Gorakhpur is the headquarters of the North Eastern Railway zone. Bhubaneshwar serves East Coast Railway, Hajipur falls under East Central Railway, and Guwahati is linked to Northeast Frontier Railway.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of the following statements :
Statement 'A' : Majority portion of Maharashtra Plateau is occupied by 'Basalt' rock.
Statement 'B' : The origin of Maharashtra Plateau is due to deposition of lava.

options.B: Statement 'A' is true, but statement 'B' is false
options.C: Statement 'A' is false, but statement 'B' is true

questions.explanation: The right pick is option A. The Maharashtra Plateau is largely capped by basalt from the Deccan Trap lava flows, and its origin is volcanic deposition — so both statements hold. Calling it sedimentary or denying the lava origin would miss the trap geology.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of following statements :
Statement 'A': The climate of Konkan is cold, uneven and dry.
Statement 'B': The climate of Maharashtra Plateau is hot, even and humid.

options.C: Statement 'A' is true, but statement 'B' is false.
options.D: Statement 'A' is false, but statement 'B' is true.

questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Konkan gets heavy monsoon rain and stays hot and humid, not cold, uneven, and dry — so statement A is false. The plateau is hotter and more seasonal than the coast but is drier and not humid like Konkan — statement B is also false.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of the following statements :
Statement 'A': While going from mean sea level to upward side, the temperature of air decreases. It is called Normal Temperature Lapse Rate.
Statement 'B': While going from mean sea level to upward side, the air temperature increases instead of decreasing. It is called inversion of temperature.

options.C: Statement 'A' is true, but statement 'B' is false.
options.D: Statement 'A' is false, but statement 'B' is true.

questions.explanation: Go with option A. Temperature normally falls with height at the environmental lapse rate, and when it rises instead you get a temperature inversion — both definitions in the stem are standard textbook statements.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of the following statements :
Statement 'A' : If availability of natural resources is in a large scale and the size of population is small in an area, such type of population is called over population.
Statement 'B' : If availability of natural resources is in a small scale and the size of population is in a large scale in an area, such type of population is called minimum population.

options.C: Statement 'A' is true, but statement 'B' is false.
options.D: Statement 'A' is false, but statement 'B' is true.

questions.explanation: Pick option B. More resources with fewer people is under-population, not over-population — statement A reverses the term. Large population on scarce resources is over-population, not 'minimum population' — statement B mislabels it too. Both definitions are wrong as printed.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of the following statements :
Statement 'A' : In winter season, the air temperature is very low and due to this, the air pressure is very high in North India as compared to Peninsular India.
Statement 'B' : In winter season, the air temperature is very high and due to this, the air pressure is very low in Peninsular India as compared to North India.

options.C: Statement 'A' is true, but statement 'B' is false.
options.D: Statement 'A' is false, but statement 'B' is true.

questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. In winter the northern plains cool sharply, so air sinks and pressure stays high there; peninsular India stays comparatively warmer, so pressure is lower — both statements describe the same land–sea temperature contrast that drives the winter circulation.

questions.text: _______ is a research centre of India located in Antarctica.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Maitri is India's permanent Antarctic research station; Aryabhatta and Rohini were satellites, and Indira Point is the southernmost tip of the Andaman–Nicobar chain, not a polar base.

questions.text: Water holding capacity is more in Regur soil and hence is excellent for _______ crop.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Regur — black cotton soil — holds moisture well in the Deccan trap belt, which is why cotton is the classic crop on it; rubber and coffee need humid tropics, jute wants alluvial floodplains.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs :
a. Tapi - I. Panchganga
b. Godavari - II. Indrayani
c. Bhima - III. Panzara
d. Krishna - IV. Pravara
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Panzara joins the Tapi, Pravara the Godavari, Indrayani the Bhima, and Panchganga the Krishna — the a–III, b–IV, c–II, d–I map. Mixing Krishna and Godavari tributaries is the usual trap.

questions.text: In _______ area is found a dense population where secondary activities are concentrated.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Pimpri–Chinchwad sits in the Pune industrial belt where manufacturing and allied services cluster, so secondary-sector jobs pull in a dense workforce — unlike the mainly agrarian Latur–Osmanabad or Pandharpur–Solapur stretches.

questions.text:
Which of the following is not a method of estimating national income?
a. Product Method
b. Export-Import Method
c. Income Method
d. Expenditure Method
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. National income is estimated by the Product, Income, and Expenditure methods — not by a standalone Export–Import method; trade flows enter indirectly through those three approaches.

questions.text:
The Budget of the Central Government is divided in two parts, namely Revenue Account and Capital Account. Which are the two sources of revenue receipts to the Central Government?
a. External Loan
b. Tax Revenue
c. Small Savings
d. Non-tax Revenue
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Revenue receipts are what the Centre earns without creating a repayment liability — tax revenue and non-tax revenue (fees, dividends, etc.). External loans and small savings are financing items, not revenue receipts.

questions.text: The Second Plan based on which of the following models emphasized the development of capital goods industries and basic industries?
questions.explanation: Pick option D. The Second Five Year Plan (1956–61) followed P. C. Mahalanobis's model, prioritising heavy industry, capital goods, and basic industries over the First Plan's agriculture-first tone.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. The Reserve Bank of India is the main agency for implementing the monetary policy.
b. To boost economic development is the aim of monetary policy.
c. Bank Rate is an instrument of monetary policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. RBI implements monetary policy, its broad aim is to support development while keeping price stability, and bank rate is a classic policy lever — all three statements hold.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. A surplus budget may prove useful during the period of inflation.
b. A deficit budget is useful for removing unemployment.
c. In India, the Agricultural Ministry is responsible for framing the budget of the Union Government.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. A surplus budget can cool inflation and a deficit can lift demand when jobs are scarce — (a) and (b) are fine. Only statement (c) is incorrect: the Union budget is framed by the Ministry of Finance, not the Agriculture Ministry.

questions.text:
Match the following :
a. Nationalization of the major banks - I. 1976 Act
b. Establishment of RRBs - II. 1998
c. The conversion of the Imperial Bank of India into the State Bank - III. July, 1969
d. Narasimham Committee Report II - IV. July, 1955
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Major banks were nationalised in July 1969, RRBs came under the 1976 Act, the Imperial Bank became SBI in July 1955, and Narasimham Committee Report II appeared in 1998 — a–III, b–I, c–IV, d–II.

questions.text: Which of the following was the nodal agency in the Government of India for estimation of Poverty ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. For decades the Planning Commission was the nodal body that set poverty lines and coordinated estimates; NSS supplied survey data, while Gadgil and Kothari committees dealt with education, not poverty measurement.

questions.text: Which of the following self employment programmes was launched during 1983-84, and was later incorporated into the Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana (PMRY)?

options.C: Self Employment for Educated Urban Youth Programme (SEEUY)
options.D: Self Employment for the Rural Poor

questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. SEEUY — Self Employment for Educated Urban Youth — was launched in 1983–84 for educated urban job-seekers and was later folded into PMRY; USEP and UWSP were urban components under a different scheme structure.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. In October 1976, an organisation named Controller General of Accounts was set up.
b. The Controller General of Accounts prepares a condensed form of the Appropriation Accounts and Financial Accounts of the Union Government.
c. The appropriation audit and regulatory audit are the statutory duties of the CGA.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to option A before MPSC withdrew the item; CGA handles government accounts while statutory audit rests with the CAG, so the role split in the stem is easy to misinterpret under exam pressure.

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are the instruments of fiscal policy ?
a. Foreign investment
b. Taxes
c. Public expenditure
d. Bank Rate Policy (BRP)
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Fiscal policy works through government taxes and public spending; bank rate belongs to monetary policy, and foreign investment is an open-economy flow, not a core fiscal instrument.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) aims at creating self employment opportunities in rural areas.
b. Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana aims at creating employment opportunities for both self employment and wage employment in urban areas.
c. In August 2011, the Parliament passed a new Act known as Mahatma Gandhi National Urban Employment Guarantee Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explanation: Go with option C. REGP targeted rural self-employment and SJSRY covered urban self- and wage-employment — both are standard textbook pairs. Statement (c) invents an urban MGNUEGA; India's guarantee act is rural MGNREGA, not an urban clone.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements according to demographic transition :
a. In Stage I an economy is primitive and backward.
b. In Stage II rapid growth of population takes place.
c. In Stage III fast industrialisation and urbanisation take place.
d. India entered into Stage II after 1921.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explanation: Pick option D. Stage I is high birth and death rates in a backward economy; Stage II sees death rates fall and population surge; Stage III follows industrialisation and urbanisation; and India's demographic transition is dated from the 1921 census — all four fit.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
a. An Auditor cannot check each and every transaction.
b. Audit evidence is not conclusive in nature.
c. An Auditor has to rely upon experts.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Auditors sample transactions rather than checking every voucher, audit evidence is persuasive not absolute proof, and specialists are relied on where technical knowledge is needed — all three are basic audit premises.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1st April, 1935.
b. The RBI was nationalised in 1950.
c. The one-rupee note and coins of all denominations are issued by the Ministry of Finance of the Government of India.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. RBI began on 1 April 1935 and one-rupee notes are issued by the Finance Ministry — both fine. Only (b) slips: nationalisation came in January 1949, not 1950.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are set up to promote exports.
b. The Finance Minister Shri Narasimha Rao introduced the new Economic Policy in 1991.
c. The Government has introduced the concept of agri export zones to encourage agricultural exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. SEZs were set up to boost exports and agri export zones were created to push farm exports — (a) and (c) hold. Statement (b) mislabels Narasimha Rao as Finance Minister; Dr. Manmohan Singh held that post when the 1991 reforms were unveiled.

questions.text: If two resistances are connected in series, then its equivalent resistance is 45 Ω and if the same resistances are connected in parallel, then its equivalent resistance is 10 Ω. What are the values of these resistances ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. If r₁ + r₂ = 45 and r₁r₂ = 450 from the parallel formula, the roots are 15 Ω and 30 Ω — the only pair that satisfies both series and parallel readings.

questions.text: When a ray of white light passes through a prism, it is separated into rays of constituent colours or wavelengths. This phenomenon is called ________
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. A prism splits white light into its colour spectrum because each wavelength bends by a different amount — that separation is dispersion, not mere reflection, refraction of a single beam, or diffraction.

questions.text: If 0.2 A current is passed for 1 minute through an electric iron whose resistance is 100 Ω, then how many joules of heat are produced ?
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Heat H = I²Rt = (0.2)² × 100 × 60 = 240 joules — current squared, resistance, and one full minute (60 s) multiplied through.

questions.text: In the long form of the periodic table, the diagonal relationship is found between the following pairs of elements :
questions.explanation: Go with option D. Diagonal neighbours in the periodic table — Li with Mg, Be with Al, and B with Si — show similar properties despite different groups; all three pairs listed in the stem qualify.

questions.text:
The wavelength of a ball of mass 257 g moving with the velocity 257 m/s will be ______ m.
Given : h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J/s
questions.explanation: Pick option A. de Broglie wavelength λ = h/(mv) = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ ÷ (0.257 × 257) ≈ 10⁻³⁵ m — macroscopic mass makes the wave nature vanishingly small, which is why the ball's wavelength is of that order.

questions.text: The total number of sigma bonds involved in ethylene molecule is
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Ethylene (C₂H₄) has one sigma bond in the C=C link and four C–H sigma bonds — five sigma bonds in all; the second bond of the double bond is pi, not sigma.

questions.text: Organ level of organization is found in which of the following phyla ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Platyhelminthes (flatworms) show organ-level organisation — organs formed from tissues. Porifera and Protozoa stay at cellular level; Coelenterata reach tissue level only.

questions.text: The correct number of Terga (T) and Sterna (S) in the abdomen of cockroach are
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. In the cockroach abdomen there are ten tergites (T) but only nine visible sternites (S) — the first sternum is absent or fused — so T-10, S-9.

questions.text: Malleus, Incus and Stapes are also called
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Malleus (hammer), incus (anvil), and stapes (stirrup) are the three middle-ear ossicles that transmit sound vibrations to the inner ear.

questions.text: Yellow-green algae is known as
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Yellow-green algae belong to the class Xanthophyceae; Chlorophyceae are green, Cyanophyceae blue-green, and Phaeophyceae brown algae.

questions.text: The group of fungi Mucorales is called
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Fungi of the order Mucorales — Mucor, Rhizopus, and allies — are commonly called black molds because of their dark sporangia on bread and other substrates.

questions.text: Bunchy top disease is most common in ______ crop.
questions.explanation: Go with option D. Bunchy top of banana, caused by the banana bunchy top virus, stunts the plant and bunches leaves at the crown — it is a classic banana disease, not papaya or citrus.

questions.text: UIP was launched in India in the year 1985 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. UIP stands for
questions.explanation: Pick option A. UIP stands for the Universal Immunization Programme, launched in 1985 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to vaccinate children against six vaccine-preventable diseases.

questions.text: The 12D treatment on food refers to

options.A: Heat treatment sufficient to kill 12 bacteria.
options.B: The use of 12 (twelve) different treatments to preserve food.
options.C: A 10¹² reduction of Clostridium botulinum endospores.
options.D: Any process that destroys thermophilic bacteria.

questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. In commercial sterilisation, '12D' means a 10¹²-fold reduction in Clostridium botulinum endospores — the standard safety target for low-acid canned foods.

questions.text: In the process of clotting, the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin

options.A: Is the final step of clotting process that involves multiple clotting factors
options.B: Occurs when fibrinogen is released from broken platelets
options.C: Is linked to hypertension and may damage artery walls
options.D: Is likely to occur too often in an individual with haemophilia

questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin strands — the final common step that weaves the clot after the cascade of clotting factors has run.

questions.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the question :
N, U, E, G, I, S and X are seven students studying in three different colleges. Minimum two are studying in each college. Each of them has a favourite subject from English, History, Geography, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology, not necessarily in the same order.
E's favourite subject is Physics and studies in college number 2 with only N. I does not study in college number 2 and he likes English. G studies in college number 3 and does not like Mathematics. Those who like Geography and Chemistry, study in the same college. X likes Biology and does not study in college number 1. S does not study with I. S does not like Chemistry. N does not like History.
In which college does 'S' study ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. College 2 holds only E and N; X (Biology) must sit in college 3 with G, and placing S there too satisfies every clue — I stays in college 1 with U, away from S.

questions.text: In a certain code language, the word LANGUAGE is written as NDPJWDIH. How will be the word OFFICIAL be written in that code ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Each letter shifts alternately +2 and +3 (L→N, A→D, N→P …); applying the same rule to OFFICIAL gives QIHLELCO.

questions.text:
Select the correct option in place of the question mark, if the same rule is followed in all the three figures.
[Diagram: three circles each divided into top-left, top-right and bottom sections]
Circle 1 — top-left: 38, top-right: 25, bottom: 9
Circle 2 — top-left: 59, top-right: 18, bottom: ?
Circle 3 — top-left: 89, top-right: 16, bottom: 15
questions.explanation: MPSC officially cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The official answer was option A (11); the three-section circle pattern in the paper is not settled enough for a fair scored item, so no mark was awarded.

questions.text:
Which of the following options will occur in place of the question mark in the given number series ?
26, 50, 82, ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. The gaps grow by 8 each time — +24, +32, then +40 — so 82 + 40 = 122 completes the series 26, 50, 82, 122.

questions.text:
In the given number series, which number will replace the question mark ?
11, 5, 20, 12, 38, ?, 74, 54
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Two interleaved series: odd positions 11, 20, 38, 74 rise by 9, 18, 36 (doubling gaps); even positions 5, 12, 26, 54 follow +7, +14, +28 — so 26 fills the blank.

questions.text:
A, B, C, D and E are standing facing to the north in a playground such as given below :
a. B is at 40 m to the right of D.
b. A is at 60 m to the south of B.
c. C is at a distance of 25 m to the west of D.
d. E is at a distance of 90 m to the north of A.
Who is in the North-east of the person, who is to the left of B ?
questions.explanation: Go with option D. Plot the positions: D and C lie west of B, so the person to the left of B is D; E sits north-east of D at (40, 30) while B, A, and C fall in other directions.

questions.text: If PEN = 70, BOOK = 86, then DUSTER = ?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Each word total equals twice the sum of its letter values (A=1 … Z=26): PEN → 35×2 = 70, BOOK → 43×2 = 86, so DUSTER → 87×2 = 174.

questions.text: A person is standing on a railway bridge which is 180 m long. A train crosses that person in 8 sec and the bridge in 20 sec. Find the speed and length of the train ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. If train length is L, L/8 = (L+180)/20 gives L = 120 m; speed = 120 ÷ 8 = 15 m/s — the same rate whether it passes the person or the full bridge.

questions.text:
Study the positions of the cube shown below and find the number on the opposite face of 1.
[Diagram: four cube orientations — (1) top 4, front-left 5, front-right 3; (2) top 1, front-left 6, front-right 2; (3) top 4, front-left 3, front-right 6; (4) top 5, front-left 2, front-right 3]
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. From the four cube views, 1 shares edges with 2 and 6 on one face and never appears opposite 3; tracing adjacent faces across the diagrams leaves 3 on the face opposite 1.

questions.text: 60% of 1600 is equal to 80% of x. Then find the value of x.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. 60% of 1600 = 960, and 960 is 80% of x, so x = 960 ÷ 0.8 = 1200.

questions.text: A tap can fill a water tank in 4 hours. Due to leakage at the bottom, it is filled in 6 hours. When the tank is full, in how much time will it get empty by the leakage ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Net fill rate 1/6 = 1/4 − 1/L, so leakage alone empties a full tank in 1 ÷ (1/4 − 1/6) = 12 hours.

questions.text: Two ships A and B start their journey from two islands which are 155 nautical miles apart. The ship A is to the west of the ship B and starts its journey to the east with the speed of 25 nautical miles per hour. At the same time, ship B starts its journey to the south with the speed of 20 nautical miles per hour. After 3 hours, what is the distance between the two ships?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. After 3 hours A has closed 75 miles of the 155-mile gap (80 miles left east–west) and B is 60 miles south — distance = √(80² + 60²) = 100 nautical miles.

questions.text: A work is completed by 20 workers in 15 days by working 6 hours per day. How many days will it take to complete the same work by 15 workers by working 8 hours per day?
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Total work is fixed: 20 × 15 × 6 = 15 × D × 8 gives D = 1800 ÷ 120 = 15 days — fewer workers but longer hours per day balance out.

questions.text: x and y are inversely proportional. When x = 3, then y = 4, so when x = 9, find the value of y.
questions.explanation: Go with option D. x and y are inversely proportional, so xy = 12; when x = 9, y = 12 ÷ 9 = 4/3.

questions.text: The cost of cashews is ₹ 1,000 per kg and that of walnuts is ₹ 1,200 per kg. If the mixture of cashews and walnuts is sold at ₹ 1,050 per kg, then what is the ratio of the walnuts to the cashews in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. By alligation, walnut: cashew = (1050 − 1000): (1200 − 1050) = 50: 150 = 1: 3 — one part walnut to three parts cashew at the ₹ 1,050 selling price.

questions.text: Newly inducted submarine INS Kalvari is developed with the help of which country ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. INS Kalvari, the first of the Scorpène-class submarines, was built at Mazagon Dock with French design and technology transfer from Naval Group (DCNS) — not the US, Japan, or Israel.

questions.text: Christiano Ronaldo, who won a record equalling fifth Ballon d'Or award for the year's best player, currently plays for which of the following clubs ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Cristiano Ronaldo won a record-equalling fifth Ballon d'Or in December 2017 while still at Real Madrid; he joined Juventus only in the summer of 2018.

questions.text: Which State in India has recently (February, 2018) announced the Policy of Financial Technology (Fintech) ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Maharashtra announced India's first dedicated Fintech Policy in February 2018 to promote Mumbai as a financial-technology hub — a standard current-affairs fact from that prelim cycle.

questions.text: Global Entrepreneurship Summit, 2017 was organised in which city of India ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The Global Entrepreneurship Summit 2017, co-hosted by India and the US, was held in Hyderabad with Ivanka Trump leading the US delegation — not Mumbai, Delhi, or Varanasi.

questions.text: France won their 10th Davis Cup title defeating which country in the Final ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. France lifted its 10th Davis Cup in November 2017 by beating Belgium 3–2 in the final at Lille — Germany, Italy, and the USA were earlier-round opponents, not the final foe.

questions.text: Which of the following IAS officers was recently (Jan. 2018) appointed as a Director General of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) ?
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to Poma Tudu (A), but Neelam Kapur was appointed DG of SAI in January 2018; MPSC withdrew the item rather than score one letter.

questions.text: Which film was awarded with the 'Golden Peacock' Award in the 48th Indian International Film Festival ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. '120 Beats per Minute' (Robin Campillo) won the Golden Peacock for Best Film at the 48th IFFI in Goa (2017); the other titles were in competition but did not take the top prize.

questions.text: Who among the following bagged the IFFI Lifetime Achievement Award in 2017 ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Canadian filmmaker Atom Egoyan received the IFFI Lifetime Achievement Award at the 48th edition in 2017; Amitabh Bachchan and the other names were not that year's honoree.

questions.text: Which of the following options is associated with the 'TAPI' Project ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. TAPI stands for Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India, a planned natural-gas pipeline project — not hydroelectricity, petroleum supply, or atomic energy.

questions.text: 'SAUBHAGYA' scheme is concerned with which of the following ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. SAUBHAGYA (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) aims at universal household electrification — every home gets a power connection, not transport, roads, or banking reform.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the options given below :
a. Former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh was chosen as the recipient of this year's Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development.
b. He received the award for "improving India's stature in the world" and for his "contributions to the cause of economic and social development."
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Statement (b) correctly cites the citation for Manmohan Singh's Indira Gandhi Prize — improving India's world stature and economic and social development; statement (a) is treated as incorrect in the official answer's reading of 'this year' — follow the official answer for scoring.

questions.text: What is the name of the rocket launched by SpaceX, under its first ever Private Mars mission ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. SpaceX's Falcon Heavy carried out its maiden flight in February 2018, including a test payload on a Mars-orbit trajectory — Tesla was the car aboard, not the rocket's name.

questions.text: Bandhan Express runs between which of the following countries ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Bandhan Express links Kolkata (India) with Khulna (Bangladesh), launched in November 2017 to strengthen rail ties — not Nepal, Pakistan, or Bhutan routes.

questions.text: Name the first State in India to operationalise a law that makes social audit of government programmes and schemes as a part of government practice.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Meghalaya became the first state to operationalise a law making social audit of government schemes mandatory in practice — Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra followed later.

questions.text: Yeshi Dhonden was honoured with Padma Shri, by the Government of India. He was honoured for his contribution in

options.D: Building a hospital in a remote hilly area

questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Tibetan physician Yeshi Dhonden received the Padma Shri for decades of work in traditional Tibetan medicine — not neonatal care, snake-bite remedies, or hospital building alone.

questions.text: Karnataka is not a party to which of the following water disputes ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. The Vansadhara river dispute is between Odisha and Andhra Pradesh — Karnataka is not a party; it is directly involved in Krishna, Mahadayi, and Godavari tribunal matters.

questions.text: According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, which Article is the soul of the Indian Constitution ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because it guarantees the right to constitutional remedies — without it, other fundamental rights would be hollow.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs about the subject and the respective list under the Constitution of India is not correctly matched ?

options.C: Post Office Saving Bank – Union List

questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Stock Exchange falls under the Union List (Entry 48), not the Concurrent List; Forest, Post Office Savings Bank, and Public Health are matched correctly in the other pairs.

questions.text: Vijay Gokhale has been appointed as the Foreign Secretary of India. Which of the following statements is incorrect about him ?

options.A: Gokhale is an IFS officer of the 1981 batch.
options.B: Gokhale is considered as an expert on China.
options.C: Gokhale is the second Marathi officer to take charge as Foreign Secretary of India.

questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Vijay Gokhale (IFS 1981), an expert on China, became Foreign Secretary in 2018 — but he hails from Pune, not Mumbai; the other three statements about batch, China expertise, and Marathi-officer status hold.

questions.text: Which of the following was selected as Constitutional Advisor during the making of the Indian Constitution ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. B.N. Rau served as Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly; Ayyangar, Mukherjee, and Jayakar held other drafting roles but not that specific title.

questions.text: Which amendment in Indian Constitution added Fundamental Duties ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (Article 51A) on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation — not the 44th, 61st, or 24th amendments.

questions.text: Anti-Defection law was passed by the Parliament by which Constitutional Amendment Act ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. The Anti-Defection law was inserted by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Tenth Schedule) — the 44th and 42nd amendments dealt with other constitutional changes.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
a. M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India.
b. Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.
c. Attorney General has the right to speak, vote and to take part in the proceedings of both the Houses of the Parliament.
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Statements (a) and (b) are correct: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General, and the AG enjoys audience in all courts; only (c) is wrong — the AG may speak in Parliament but cannot vote in either House.

questions.text: According to which Article of the Indian Constitution, are the State and Union Public Service Commissions established ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Article 315 provides for a Union Public Service Commission and a Public Service Commission for each state — Articles 318–320 spell out composition, removal, and functions.

questions.text: According to which Article of the Indian Constitution, is the Council of Ministers responsible to the Lok Sabha ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Article 75(3) lays down that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha — Article 74 covers aid and advice to the President; 73 is Union executive power, 76 the Attorney General.

title: MPSC गट-क सेवा संयुक्त पूर्व परीक्षा 2018 (मराठी)

questions.text: 1857 च्या उठावानंतर भारताचा कारभार चालविण्यासाठी कोणत्या पदाची निर्मिती करण्यात आली ?
questions.explanation: परीक्षकाने पर्याय A चिन्हांकित केला. Government of India Act 1858 ने Company rule संपवले आणि भारतीय प्रशासनावर नियंत्रण ठेवण्यासाठी British cabinet मध्ये Secretary of State for India हे पद केले — 1857 नंतरचे नवीन शिखर. Lieutenant Governor, Chief Commissioner provincial पातळीवर आधीच होते; External Affairs Minister आधुनिक पद.

questions.text:
जोड्या जुळवा :
अ. दीनबंधू मित्र - I. बारडोली सत्याग्रह
ब. बाबा रामचंद्र - II. मुळशी सत्याग्रह
क. सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल - III. अयोध्येच्या शेतकऱ्यांचा लढा
ड. सेनापती बापट - IV. 'नीलदर्पण' नाटक
questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय C येतो. Dinabandhu Mitra — 'Nil Darpan' नाटक (a–IV); Baba Ramchandra — Ayodhya शेतकरी संघर्ष (b–III); Sardar Patel — Bardoli Satyagraha (c–I); Senapati Bapat — Mulshi Satyagraha (d–II). Patel आणि Bapat च्या satyagraha अदलबदल — सामान्य फसवणूक.

questions.text:
'इंडियन असोशिएशन' या संस्थेविषयी कोणती विधाने बरोबर आहेत ?
अ. संस्था स्थापन करण्यासाठी दादाभाई नौरोजी यांनी पुढाकार घेतला होता.
ब. हिंदू व मुसलमान यांच्यात मित्रत्वाची भावना निर्माण करण्याचा हेतू होता.
क. फिरोजशाह मेहता व के.टी. तेलंग यांनी संस्था चालविली.
ड. सिव्हिल सर्व्हिस परीक्षेकरिता वयोमर्यादा वाढविण्यासाठी प्रयत्न केले.
