questions.explanation: येथे खात्रीशीर उत्तर पर्याय A. Tibetan physician Yeshi Dhonden ला traditional Tibetan medicine साठी Padma Shri; neonatal care, snake-bite, hospital building एकटे नाही.

questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणत्या पाणीवाटप तंट्यामध्ये कर्नाटकचा समावेश नाही ?
questions.explanation: परीक्षकाने पर्याय A चिन्हांकित केला. Vansadhara dispute Odisha–Andhra Pradesh — Karnataka party नाही; Krishna, Mahadayi, Godavari tribunal मध्ये सहभागी.

questions.text: डॉ. बी.आर. आंबेडकरांनी संविधानाच्या कोणत्या कलमास भारतीय संविधानाचा आत्मा मानले आहे ?
questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय D येतो. Dr. Ambedkar Article 32 ला Constitution चे 'heart and soul' म्हणाले — constitutional remedies; त्याशिवाय इतर fundamental rights रिकामे.

questions.text: भारताच्या संविधानाच्या अंतर्गत विषय आणि सूची यांच्या जोड्यांपैकी कोणती जोडी अयोग्य आहे, ते ठरवा.

options.C: पोस्ट ऑफिस बचत बँक – केंद्र सूची

questions.explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय B. Stock Exchange Union List (Entry 48) — Concurrent List नाही; Forest, Post Office Savings Bank, Public Health इतर जोड्या बरोबर.

questions.text: विजय गोखले यांची भारताच्या परराष्ट्र सचिव नुकतीच नेमणूक करण्यात आली आहे. त्यांच्या संदर्भात खालीलपैकी कोणते विधान चुकीचे आहे ?

options.A: गोखले हे भारतीय परराष्ट्र सेवेच्या 1981 च्या तुकडीचे अधिकारी आहेत.
options.B: गोखले हे चीनविषयक प्रश्नांचे तज्ञ मानले जातात.
options.C: परराष्ट्र सचिवपद भूषविणारे ते दुसरे मराठी अधिकारी आहेत.

questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय D. Vijay Gokhale (IFS 1981), China expert, 2018 Foreign Secretary — Pune वरून, Mumbai नाही; batch, China expertise, Marathi-officer status बरोबर.

questions.text: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या निर्मिती दरम्यान संविधान सल्लागार म्हणून कोणाची नियुक्ती केली गेली ?
questions.explanation: येथे खात्रीशीर उत्तर पर्याय A. B.N. Rau Constituent Assembly चे Constitutional Advisor; Ayyangar, Mukherjee, Jayakar इतर drafting roles — ते title नाही.

questions.text: कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे मूलभूत कर्तव्यांचा भारतीय राज्यघटनेत समावेश करण्यात आला ?
questions.explanation: परीक्षकाने पर्याय A चिन्हांकित केला. Fundamental Duties 42nd Amendment 1976 (Article 51A) — Swaran Singh Committee; 44th, 61st, 24th नाही.

questions.text: संसदेने पक्षांतरबंदी कायदा कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्ती कायद्यानुसार संमत केला आहे ?
questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय B येतो. Anti-Defection law 52nd Amendment 1985 (Tenth Schedule); 44th, 42nd इतर constitutional changes.

questions.text:
खालील विधाने लक्षात घ्या :
अ. एम.सी. सेटलवाड हे भारताचे पहिले महान्यायवादी होते.
ब. महान्यायवाद्यास भारताच्या सर्व न्यायालयात उपस्थित राहण्याचा अधिकार आहे.
क. महान्यायवादी संसदेच्या दोन्ही सभागृहांच्या कामकाजात सहभागी होतो. त्याला तिथे बोलणे व मत देण्याचा अधिकार आहे.
वरीलपैकी कोणते विधान/विधाने चूक आहेत ?
questions.explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय C. (a), (b) बरोबर — M.C. Setalvad first AG, सर्व courts मध्ये audience; (c) चुकीचे — AG Parliament मध्ये बोलू शकतो, vote करू शकत नाही.

questions.text: केंद्र व राज्य लोकसेवा आयोगाची स्थापना भारतीय राज्यघटनेतील कोणत्या कलमान्वये करण्यात आलेली आहे ?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय D. Article 315 — Union PSC आणि प्रत्येक राज्यासाठी PSC; Article 318–320 composition, removal, functions.

questions.text: भारतीय संविधानाच्या कोणत्या अनुच्छेदानुसार मंत्री परिषद लोकसभेला उत्तरदायी असते ?
questions.explanation: येथे खात्रीशीर उत्तर पर्याय A. Article 75(3) — Council of Ministers collectively Lok Sabha ला जबाबदार; Article 74 President ला aid/advice; 73 Union executive power, 76 Attorney General.

questions.text:
'Green Peace and Air Visual Analysis of Pollution' report declared the most polluted cities of World. Among 30 most polluted cities consists 22 cities of India. Arrange the following cities in increasing order of ranking in Air pollution.
(a) Delhi (b) Noida (c) Gurugram (d) Gaziabad
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. In the Greenpeace and AirVisual 2018 World Air Quality Report, Gurugram, Ghaziabad, Noida, and Delhi all sat among the world's most polluted cities — the official answer orders them as Gurugram → Ghaziabad → Noida → Delhi in increasing rank order. Pollution rankings shift year to year, so treat this as the 2018-report sequence the paper expects.

questions.text: Kazakhstan renames it's capital 'Astana' after its first President to honour him. The name of the new capital is _______
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. In March 2019 Kazakhstan renamed its capital Astana to Nursultan, honouring its first President Nursultan Nazarbayev. Tokayev succeeded him as President; Nazarbayev is the person honoured, not the new city name itself.

questions.text:
Select the correct statements - (Padma Award, 2019)
(a) Tijanbai and Anil Kumar Naik were honoured by Padma Vibhushan Award.
(b) Dharampal Gulati and Bachendri Pal were honoured by Padma Bhushan Award.
(c) S. Thimakka and Devendra Swaroop were honoured by Padma Bhushan Award.
(d) Manoj Vajpayee and Sudam Kate were honoured by Padma Shri Award.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Padma Vibhushan 2019 went to Teejan Bai and Anil Manibhai Naik; Padma Bhushan to Dharampal Gulati and Bachendri Pal; Padma Shri to Manoj Bajpayee and Sudam Kate. Statement (c) is incorrect because Saalumarada Thimmakka and Devendra Swarup received Padma Shri, not Padma Bhushan.

questions.text: Select the incorrect statement - (Seoul Peace Prize)

options.A: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was honoured by 'Seoul Peace Prize'.
options.B: Narendra Modi donated two lakh dollar (Prize Amount) to Namami Gange Campaign.
options.C: Seoul Peace Prize was initiated on 1995.
options.D: Kofi Annan, Angela Merkel were also Seoul Peace Prize winners.

questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. Narendra Modi did win the Seoul Peace Prize 2018 and donated the prize money to Namami Gange; past winners include Kofi Annan and Angela Merkel. The trap is statement (c): the prize was established in 1990, not 1995.

questions.text: ______ became second male tennis player to win 100 singles titles.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Roger Federer became only the second man in the Open Era to reach 100 ATP singles titles, after Jimmy Connors. Nadal and Tsitsipas were active rivals but had not crossed that century mark when this question was set.

questions.text:
Match the pairs :
Book - Author
(a) Capital in the Twenty First Century - (i) Caroline Criedo Perez
(b) Pocket Piketty - (ii) Kevine Orarchy
(c) A Short History of Brexit - (iii) Jesper Roine
(d) Invisible Women - Exposing a Data Bias in a world design for men - (iv) Thomas Piketty
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Thomas Piketty wrote 'Capital in the Twenty-First Century'; Jesper Roine condensed it as 'Pocket Piketty'; Kevin O'Rourke authored 'A Short History of Brexit'; Caroline Criado Perez wrote 'Invisible Women'. The paper spells some names loosely — match on the well-known titles.

questions.text:
Which statement/s is/are false about proposed 'Bullet Train' ?
(a) High speed Railway project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad.
(b) Technical assistance and easy loan by Japan.
(c) 20,000 people will get employment during construction.
(d) World Bank will provide full loan for project.
questions.explanation: Pick option B. The Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train is a Japanese-assisted high-speed project expected to employ thousands during construction. Only statement (d) is false — finance comes mainly from Japan, not a full World Bank loan.

questions.text: Indian team has won the under 19 cricket world cup competition on 2018. For how many times the under 19 Indian cricket team has won the world cup ?
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. India's Under-19 team lifted the World Cup in 2018 at New Zealand — their fourth title after wins in 2000, 2008, and 2012. Third or fifth sounds close but miscounts one edition.

questions.text:
Select the correct statement/s :
(a) Pakyang Airport is the First Airport in Himalayan State.
(b) Pakyang Airport is the 100th Airport in the India.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Pakyong Airport in Sikkim, inaugurated in September 2018, was celebrated as India's 100th operational airport. Statement (a) overreaches — Himalayan states like Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal already had airports before Sikkim got one.

questions.text:
Match the pairs : (91st Oscar Award)
Category - Film
(a) Best Film - (i) Bao
(b) Best Short Film - (ii) Roma
(c) Best Animated Short Film - (iii) Green Book
(d) Best Foreign Film - (iv) Skin
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. At the 91st Oscars, 'Green Book' won Best Picture, 'Skin' Best Live Action Short, 'Bao' Best Animated Short, and 'Roma' Best Foreign Language Film. Best Picture and Best Foreign Film are the pair most students mix up.

questions.text: Shruti Shrikhande has topped among girls in combined defence services examination, 2018. She hails from which of the following cities in Maharashtra ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Shruti Shrikhande from Pune topped among women in the Combined Defence Services Examination 2018, making Maharashtra news that year. Ratnagiri, Mumbai, and Nashik are plausible distractors for a state-specific current-affairs item.

questions.text:
Antonio Guterres was recently in news. Which is not true about him ?
(a) He was a Prime Minister of Portugal in 1995 - 2001.
(b) He worked as United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees from June 2005 to December 2015.
(c) He Co-chaired the First European Union - Africa Summit.
(d) He founded the Portuguese Refugee Council.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Antonio Guterres served as Portugal's Prime Minister (1995–2002), led UNHCR (2005–2015), co-chaired the first EU–Africa Summit, and helped found the Portuguese Refugee Council — every statement in the stem holds. MPSC often tests biography details of the sitting UN Secretary-General.

questions.text: In which of the following 'Mission Indra Dhanush' is concerned ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Mission Indradhanush is the Union Health Ministry's intensified immunisation drive to cover unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children and pregnant women. Water conservation, cloud seeding, and irrigation belong to entirely different missions.

questions.text: Spicejet, the first Indian low-cost air carrier joined IATA. IATA stands for :
questions.explanation: Go with option C. IATA expands to International Air Transport Association — the global trade body for airlines. SpiceJet becoming its first Indian low-cost member was headline news around 2019; 'Travel' instead of 'Transport' is the usual distractor.

questions.text: Two Nobel Prizes for 2018 and 2019 will be awarded this year in _______ category.
questions.explanation: Pick option D. The Swedish Academy postponed the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature because of a misconduct scandal, so both the 2018 and 2019 Literature prizes were awarded together in 2019. Peace, Chemistry, and Medicine followed their normal single-year schedule.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
(a) The Governor is not an integral part of the State Legislature.
(b) The Governor has no security of tenure.
(c) The Governor may be removed by the President at any time.
(d) The Constitution does not lay down any grounds upon which a Governor may be removed by the President.
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. The Governor enjoys no fixed tenure and serves at the President's pleasure, with no removal grounds spelt out in the Constitution. Statement (a) is wrong because Article 168 makes the Governor an integral part of the State Legislature.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about 'State Election Commission' :
(a) It conducted rural and urban local body elections including the election of members of Maharashtra Legislative Council elected by the members of rural and urban local bodies.
(b) The State Election Commissioner cannot be removed by the Governor, though appointed by him.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. A State Election Commissioner, though appointed by the Governor, cannot be removed at the Governor's whim — removal needs the same tough process as a High Court judge. Statement (a) is false because SEC runs panchayat and municipal polls, not Legislative Council elections from local bodies.

questions.text: Which of the following has been wrongly listed as a recommendation of the 'Sarkaria Commission' ?

options.A: It favoured change in the role of Rajya Sabha and Centre's power to reorganise the states.
options.B: It favoured sparingly use of Article 356 of the Constitution.
options.C: It turned down the demand for the abolition of the office of the Governor.
options.D: It favoured implementation of the three language formula.

questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. The Sarkaria Commission (1983) urged sparing use of Article 356, rejected abolishing the Governor's office, and backed the three-language formula. It did not recommend reshaping Rajya Sabha's role or the Centre's power to reorganise states — that option is wrongly attributed.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
(a) For creation of Legislative Council, resolution must be passed by 2/3 majority of the members of the Legislative Assembly present and voting of concerned state is necessary.
(b) For creation of Legislative Council, resolution must be passed by 2/3 majority of the members of the parliament is necessary.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Under Article 169, a state Legislative Assembly must pass a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting before Parliament can create a Legislative Council. Parliament enacts the law, but no separate two-thirds resolution of the whole Parliament is required as statement (b) claims.

questions.text:
Match the pairs :
Person - Role
(a) Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha - (i) Objectives Resolution
(b) Dr. Rajendra Prasad - (ii) Constitutional advisor of Constitutional Assembly
(c) Sir B.N. Rao - (iii) Permanent President of Constitutional Assembly
(d) Jawaharlal Nehru - (iv) Temporary President of Constitutional Assembly
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Dr Sachchidanand Sinha was the temporary (first) President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr Rajendra Prasad became its permanent President; Sir B.N. Rau served as constitutional advisor; Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution. Swapping Sinha and Nehru's roles is the common match-the-pairs trap.

questions.text:
Match the pairs :
Articles - Subject matter
(a) 243 A - (i) Elections of Panchayats
(b) 243 D - (ii) Constitution of Panchayats
(c) 243 B - (iii) Gram Sabha
(d) 243 K - (iv) Reservation of Seats
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Article 243A covers the Gram Sabha; 243B the constitution of Panchayats; 243D reservation of seats; and 243K elections to Panchayats. Mixing 243B with elections and 243K with constitution is the standard distractor layout.

questions.text: Whom does the Advocate General of the State submits his resignation ?

options.A: Chief Justice of High Court of the State
options.D: Chief Minister of the respective State

questions.explanation: Go with option B. The Advocate General of a State holds office during the Governor's pleasure and submits resignation to the Governor — the same appointing authority. The Chief Minister, Chief Justice, and President are high offices but not the constitutional addressee for this resignation.

questions.text: Which of the following writs in not specifically provided under Article-32 of the Constitution of India ?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue five writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari. 'Injunction' is a remedy under ordinary civil law, not one of the five constitutional writs listed in Article 32.

questions.text:
Which of the following provision/s is/are not contained in Article-39 of the Indian Constitution ?
(a) Equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
(b) Organisation of Village Panchayats.
(c) To secure a social order for promotion of welfare of the people.
(d) The citizens, men and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Article 39 lists DPSPs such as adequate livelihood and equal pay for equal work — so (a) and (d) belong here. Organising village panchayats sits in Article 40, and securing a welfare social order is the broader thrust of Article 38, not Article 39.

questions.text: The primary objective of judicial control over administration is :

options.A: To restrict the discretion and arbitrariness of administrative agencies.
options.B: To help in redressing the grievances of citizens.
options.C: To safeguard the rights and liberty of the citizens.
options.D: To contain and penalise the wrongful acts of government officials.

questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Judicial review over administration chiefly protects citizens' fundamental rights and liberties against arbitrary official action. Redressing grievances and checking discretion are important effects, but safeguarding rights and liberty is the primary constitutional objective textbooks cite.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true about Lord Dalhousie ?
(a) Started the Railway Era.
(b) Establishment of independent public works department.
(c) Establishment of Telegram Department in 1852.
(d) Passed post law and started postal stamps in 1854.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Lord Dalhousie's tenure is remembered for the railway age (first line 1853), an independent Public Works Department, the telegraph network from 1852, and the Post Office Act with postage stamps from 1854 — all four statements in the stem are textbook milestones.

questions.text: Indian Council of scientific studies established at __________.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. The paper's 'Indian Council of scientific studies' points to the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), founded in Calcutta in 1876 by Mahendra Lal Sircar — the cradle where C. V. Raman later did his Nobel work. Delhi, Madras, and Bangalore are later CSIR or IISc hubs, not this 1876 body.

questions.text: Which First Political Organisation was formed in Maharashtra in 1852 ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option A. The Bombay Association (1852) — led by Jagannath Shankar Seth and allied merchants — is counted as Maharashtra's first political organisation. East India Association came later in London; Sarvajanik Sabha and Bombay Presidency Association belong to subsequent decades.

questions.text: Who established the 'Prathana Samaj' in Mumbai in 1867 ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Dr. Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867 as a prayer-house reform society — monotheism, women's uplift, and social service without idol worship. Gopal Hari Deshmukh (Lokhitwadi), Naoroji, and Sitaram Desai are linked to other reform streams.

questions.text: After bearing public criticism which social reformer served lame, blind and leprosy persons ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Lokhitwadi Gopal Hari Deshmukh faced sharp public criticism for his reformist Lokhit articles in the Prabhakar, then turned to hands-on charity — serving the lame, blind, and leprosy patients. Anandibai Joshi, Anutai Wagh, and Bhau Daji Lad fit medicine or civic philanthropy elsewhere.

questions.text: Who were hanged in Jacksan Murder case ?

options.A: Krishnaji Gopal Karve, Vinayak Narayan Deshpande

questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. In the 1909 Jackson Murder case at Nashik, revolutionaries Krishnaji Gopal Karve and Vinayak Narayan Deshpande were hanged for assassinating Collector A. M. T. Jackson. The other name-pairs belong to different conspiracy or martyr episodes.

questions.text: Who is First national poet of modern India ?
questions.explanation: Go with option D. Henry Louis Vivian Derozio — leader of the Young Bengal movement and author of 'To India — My Native Land' — is textbook-listed as the first national poet of modern India. Tarkhedkar, Savarkar, and the bare 'Vinayak' label belong to Marathi-nationalist poetry, not this Anglo-Indian pioneer slot.

questions.text:
The effects of uprising of 1857 are as follow.
(a) The end of company rule
(b) The Indians were not given jobs in administration
(c) Became the inspiration for Indian Freedom struggle
(d) Reorganisation of the military
questions.explanation: Pick option C. The 1857 uprising ended East India Company rule, fired later freedom movements, and triggered a thorough military reorganisation — so (a), (c), and (d) hold. Statement (b) is the odd one out in the official answer's reading: post-1857 policy did open some Indian recruitment, even while higher posts stayed largely European.

questions.text: In which place fourth conference of Indian National Congress was held ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. The fourth session of the Indian National Congress met at Allahabad in 1888 under George Yule's presidency. Mumbai hosted the first (1885); Ahmedabad and Madras came in later years.

questions.text:
Who among the following helped Mahatma Jyotiba Phule for running girl's school ?
(a) Sakharam Yashwant Paranjape, Sadashiv Govind Hate
(b) Sadashivrao Balal Govande, Moro Vitthal Valvekar
(c) Vishnupant Thatte, Keshav Shivram Bhavalkar
(d) Devrao Thosar, Mrs. E.C. Jones
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Mahatma Jyotiba Phule's girls' schools drew support from a wide circle: Paranjape–Hate, Govande–Valvekar, Thatte–Bhavalkar, and Thosar–Mrs. E. C. Jones — all four bundles in the stem are credited in Maharashtra school history.

questions.text: In which provinces was 'Rayatwari System' started during British reign ?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option A. The Ryotwari (Rayatwari) settlement — direct revenue agreement between the cultivator and government — was chiefly applied in the Madras and Bombay presidencies. Bengal and Punjab are associated with zamindari or mahalwari systems instead.

questions.text:
In which Satyagraha Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde was participated ?
(a) Parvati Satyagraha
(b) Wai Ganapati Mandir Satyagraha
(c) Waykom Mandir Satyagraha
(d) Laxmi-Narayan Mandir Satyagraha
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde joined the Parvati Satyagraha, Wai Ganapati Mandir Satyagraha, and Vaikom (Waykom) temple-entry movement — all three appear in his reform biography. Laxmi-Narayan Mandir Satyagraha is not counted in the official answer's trio.

questions.text:
Which statements are true regarding 1935 Act ?
(a) Anglo-Indian, Indian Christian, Shikh Constituencies were created.
(b) Establishment of Federal Court.
(c) Creation of Indian High Commissioner.
(d) Rajgopalachari stated that 'Worse than dyarchy' regarding the Law.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. The Government of India Act 1935 created separate Anglo-Indian, Indian Christian, and Sikh constituencies, set up the Federal Court, and drew Rajagopalachari's 'worse than dyarchy' verdict — (a), (b), and (d). The Indian High Commissioner post dates to the 1919 Act, not 1935, so (c) drops out.

questions.text:
In the Formation of Indian National Congress the following leaders were involved.
(a) Jagannath Shankar Seth, Dadabhai Naoroji
(b) Umesh Chandra Banerjee, Sir Allan Hume
(c) Ganesh Joshi, Vinayak Savarkar
(d) Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar, Durgaram Mancharam
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to (a) and (b) — Jagannath Shankar Seth, Naoroji, Allan Hume, and Banerjee — before MPSC withdrew the item; pairing (c) wrongly lists Savarkar and (d) mixes other names, so do not count it in scoring.

questions.text:
Match the following :
a. Tarabai Shinde - I. Sharada Sadan
b. Tanhubai Birje - II. Formation of 'Hindu Ladies Social Club'
c. Pandita Ramabai - III. 'Stri-Purush Tulana' book
d. Ramabai Ranade - IV. India's First Woman Editor
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Tarabai Shinde wrote 'Stri-Purush Tulana'; Tanhubai Birje was India's first woman editor; Pandita Ramabai founded Sharada Sadan; Ramabai Ranade helped form the Hindu Ladies Social Club — the a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii map.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers generate maximum hydel power?

options.A: West flowing rivers of western ghat

questions.explanation: Go with option B. Peninsular rivers flowing east — Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri and their tributaries — carry the bulk of India's installed hydel capacity through the Western Ghats gradient and numerous dam cascades. West-flowing Konkan streams are shorter; Ganga valley and middle-India shares are smaller in comparison.

questions.text:
Match the pairs of small scale industry and their places of Maharashtra.
a. Chaddar - I. Nagpur
b. Himrushawl - II. Sawantwadi
c. Wooden Toys - III. Solapur
d. Silk Sari - IV. Aurangabad
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Solapur chaddar (blanket) weaving, Aurangabad Himru shawls, Sawantwadi wooden toys, and Nagpur silk saris are the standard Maharashtra handicraft–district pairings in state geography lists — a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i.

questions.text:
Match the pairs :
a. Tadoba - I. Nagpur
b. Pench - II. Amravati
c. Navegaon - III. Chandrapur
d. Gugamal - IV. Gondia
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Tadoba lies in Chandrapur district, Pench spans the Nagpur belt, Navegaon is in Gondia, and Gugamal (Melghat) falls in Amravati — the a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii set. Swapping Pench with Chandrapur is the usual trap.

questions.text: _______ fort is called Eastern Gibralter by Britishers.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. British gazetteers and Grant Duff called Raigad the 'Gibraltar of the East' for its sheer scarped cliffs and strategic hill-top seat of Maratha power. Janjira is a sea fort nickname distractor; Karnala and Lingana are nearby Sahyadri forts without that label.

questions.text: _______ soil is covered largest area in India.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. Alluvial soils — spread across the Indo-Gangetic plain, Brahmaputra valley, and major river deltas — cover the largest geographical area among India's soil types. Black cotton dominates the Deccan trap belt but not the national acreage total.

questions.text:
Which type of settlement pattern is having following features ?
(a) Roads are parallel to each other.
(b) Roads are rectangular to each other.
(c) Houses are in rows.
(d) Highway or Railways are crossing to each others.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Parallel and rectangular street grids, houses in rows, and a highway or railway cutting across the blocks define the chess-board (grid-iron) settlement pattern — typical of planned colonial towns and cantonments.

questions.text:
Examine the trueness of following statements.
Statement (A) : Godavari river basin is separated from Tapi river basin due to the Satmala-Ajintha mountain ranges.
Statement (B) : Godavari river basin is separated from Bhima river basin due to the Shambhu-Mahadeo mountain ranges.

options.C: Statement (A) is true and (B) is incorrect.
options.D: Statement (A) is incorrect and (B) is true.

questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Statement (A) is correct: the Satmala–Ajintha ranges divide the Godavari basin from the Tapi basin in Maharashtra. Statement (B) swaps the divider — the Shambhu–Mahadeo range does not separate Godavari from the Bhima basin in the official answer's reading.

questions.text: To the north of Maharashtra ............ mountain range and to its east ............ hills are found.
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. The Satpuda range forms Maharashtra's northern boundary, while the Gavilgad hills lie along the eastern side toward the Amravati–Chhindwara belt. Sahyadri is the western escarpment; Balaghat and Bhamragad are not the standard north–east pairing.

questions.text: River Hugli is the distributory of ............ river.
questions.explanation: Go with option C. The Hugli (Hooghly) is a distributary of the Ganga that branches westward near Farraka and flows through Kolkata to the Bay of Bengal. Damodar joins it downstream; Brahmaputra and Padma belong to the eastern Bengal system.

questions.text: Human migration from one place to other place, due to unavoidable circumstances takes place because of ............ factors.
questions.explanation: Pick option B. Migration forced by drought, famine, war, or persecution is driven by push factors — negative conditions at the origin that compel departure. Pull factors attract by choice; 'scientific factors' is not a standard migration label in geography syllabi.

questions.text: ________ state in India is a major Bauxite producing state.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. The paper spells it 'Zarkhand' — read that as Jharkhand, which sits on the eastern plateau bauxite belt and ranks among India's top bauxite producers alongside Odisha and Gujarat.

questions.text: "Operation Flood plan" is related with ________ .
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Operation Flood was NDDB's White Revolution programme to expand organised milk collection, processing, and marketing nationwide — nothing to do with flood control or poultry.

questions.text: India's first hydroelectric power station 'Shivsamudram' is on ________ river.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option A. India's first hydroelectric station (1902) was built at Shivanasamudra on the Kaveri in Karnataka — not Krishna, Tungbhadra, or Godavari.

questions.text:
Match the pairs of Column 'A' and Column 'B'.
(a) Lawyer - (i) Primary Activities
(b) Transport - (ii) Secondary Activities
(c) Flour mill - (iii) Tertiary Activities
(d) Hunting - (iv) Quaternary Activities
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Hunting draws directly from nature (primary), a flour mill processes raw grain (secondary), transport is a service (tertiary), and a lawyer offers knowledge-based advice (quaternary) — match (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

questions.text: ________ is a worlds largest 'Delta region' of India.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. The Sundarbans delta — formed where the Ganga and Brahmaputra meet the Bay of Bengal — is the world's largest delta and India's best-known deltaic tract; Vrindavan, Rajahmundry, and Machilipatnam are towns, not that scale of delta.

questions.text: Type of an Audit Programme may be ________.
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. An audit programme is planned as either fixed (standard steps for similar audits) or flexible (adapted case by case) — distinct from statutory mandate, permanence, or a single standard template.

questions.text:
The following are the beneficiaries of the integrated rural development program :
(a) Minority farmers
(b) Small landowner farmer
(c) Landless agricultural labourers
(d) Big farmers
Which of the above statement/s are correct ?
questions.explanation: Go with option C. IRDP targeted the rural poor — small and marginal farmers, landless agricultural labourers, and disadvantaged groups — not large landholders; big farmers were outside its beneficiary net.

questions.text: Generally in which of the following budget shows the Receipts and Expenditure of the Central Government ?
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The official option was Revenue budget, but receipts and expenditure appear in both revenue and capital sections of the Union Budget, so the stem is ambiguous — MPSC withdrew the item rather than score one letter.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) The purpose of Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 was to promote regional equality.
(b) In 1955 the Village and Small Scale Industries Committee also called the Karve Committee.
(c) In a small-scale industrial unit maximum investment allowed is rupees ten crore.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. IPR 1956 pushed licensed industrial growth to reduce regional imbalances, and the 1955 Karve Committee framed policy for village and small-scale industries — both (a) and (b) hold. Statement (c) is incorrect because the small-scale investment ceiling in syllabus years was far below ten crore.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) Maharashtra state has declared the organic farming policy in January 2013.
(b) Maharashtra state has introduced Krishi Sanjeevani Yojana in 2011.
(c) Maharashtra state has launched Agri-business Infrastructure Development Investment Programme with the assistance of world bank.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Maharashtra announced its organic farming policy in January 2013 and rolled out Krishi Sanjeevani Yojana in 2011 — (a) and (b) stand. The World Bank-linked agri-business infrastructure line in (c) does not match the standard Maharashtra scheme list.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) Letter of credit is a primary function of commercial bank.
(b) There is no difference between current account deposits and saving account deposits of a commercial bank.
(c) Credit money is created by the central bank of a country.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. All three statements are wrong: accepting deposits and advancing loans are the core commercial-bank functions, not letter of credit alone; current and savings accounts differ in rules and interest; and credit money is created mainly through bank lending, not by the central bank printing notes.

questions.text:
Which two of the following social factors are responsible to the high birth rate in India?
(a) Poverty
(b) Lower age at the time of marriage
(c) Predominance of agriculture
(d) Religious and social superstitions
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Early marriage widens the childbearing span, and deep-rooted religious and social customs favour larger families — (b) and (d) are the classic social drivers of high birth rates in India.

questions.text: Which commission performs the function of the distribution of financial resources at Central Level in India ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The Finance Commission recommends how tax revenue is shared between the Union and the States — the Planning Commission planned development, and UPSC recruits civil servants.

questions.text: Which of the following thing is related to the Fiscal Policy in Indian Economy ?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Fiscal policy covers government tax and non-tax revenue plus public spending — bank rate and cash reserve ratio are monetary tools, and direct action is a central-bank market operation.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
(a) World Trade Organisation was set up on 1 January 1995.
(b) The purpose of WTO is to remove restrictions in international trade.
(c) India is one of the founder member of WTO.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: On this one, option D is correct. WTO began on 1 January 1995 to liberalise world trade, and India was among the founding members — none of (a), (b), or (c) is incorrect.

questions.text: Literacy (Education) is mainly which type of the indicator of development ?
questions.explanation: Go with option A. Literacy/education measures human capital and skills — a human-resource development indicator — not purely geography, income alone, or political structure.

questions.text: Which economic problem creates in the economy due to "Deficit Finance" ?
questions.explanation: Pick option C. Deficit finance means spending beyond revenue by borrowing or printing money, which pumps extra purchasing power into the economy and tends to push up the general price level — inflation.

questions.text: How many types are of Government Budget ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Government budgets are classified into three balance types — surplus (revenue exceeds spending), deficit (spending exceeds revenue), and balanced (both equal) — the standard trio in public-finance textbooks.

questions.text: In which form "Density of population" can be measured ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Population density is always expressed as persons per square kilometre — the universal demographic unit; per hectare or per square foot are not standard census measures.

questions.text: With reference to India which of the following is another important import item after crude oil ? (Economic Survey, 2016)
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. Per the Economic Survey 2016, after crude oil, gold was India's next major import by value — jewellery demand and safe-haven buying kept bullion high on the import bill.

questions.text: If the four colours on the carbon resistor are orange, blue, yellow and gold, the resistance value is ______.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Colour bands: orange = 3, blue = 6, yellow = multiplier 10⁴, gold = ±5% tolerance — so resistance is 36 × 10⁴ Ω.

questions.text:
Match the following :
(a) Gravity - (i) Coulomb/sec
(b) Current - (ii) Ohms
(c) Velocity - (iii) m/sec²
(d) Resistance - (iv) m/sec
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Gravity is m/s², electric current is coulomb per second (ampere), velocity is m/s, and resistance is ohm — pair (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

questions.text: Out of the following which is not a planet ?
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune remain the outer gas/ice giants in the eight-planet solar system.

questions.text: Which of the following resonating structure is not correct for CO₂ ?

options.B: ⁻Ö-C≡O⁺ (single bond to left O with negative charge, triple bond to right O with positive charge)
options.C: ⁺O≡C-Ö⁻ (triple bond to left O with positive charge, single bond to right O with negative charge)
options.D: ⁻Ö-C⁺-Ö⁻ (single bonds to both oxygens, central C with positive charge, both oxygens with negative charge)

questions.explanation: Go with option C. Valid CO₂ resonance keeps the carbon skeleton symmetric; the ⁺O≡C–O⁻ form with positive charge on oxygen breaks the usual electronegativity rule and is the structure examiners mark as incorrect.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding catalyst is not true ?

options.B: Catalyst reduces the time required for reaching the equilibrium state in the reaction.
options.C: Catalyst participate in the reaction and speed it up.
options.D: Catalyst is always in the same phase as the reactants and products.

questions.explanation: Pick option D. Catalysts can be homogeneous or heterogeneous — they need not sit in the same phase as reactants; solid catalysts in liquid reactions are everyday examples. Options A–C describe genuine catalytic effects.

questions.text: Net dipole moment of carbon tetrachloride is zero because of ______.

options.C: Similar sizes of carbon and chlorine atoms
options.D: Similar electron affinities of carbon and chlorine

questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. CCl₄ has a regular tetrahedral shape with four identical C–Cl bonds pointing symmetrically; the bond dipoles cancel out, so the net dipole moment is zero — planar structure (A) is wrong for carbon.

questions.text:
Choose the correct alternative about the shark :
(a) Mouth on ventral side
(b) Viviparity
(c) Cycloid scales
(d) Cartilaginous endoskeleton
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Sharks have the mouth on the ventral side, a cartilaginous skeleton, and many species are viviparous; they bear placoid scales, not cycloid scales — so (c) drops out.

questions.text: Select correct alternative in the place of question mark. Cockroach : Malpighian tubules :: Earthworm : ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs in cockroach; in earthworm the same role is played by nephridia — typhlosole and clitellum serve other functions.

questions.text:
Some statements are given below about animals.
(a) All vertebrates are chordates.
(b) All birds fly in the air.
(c) All insects are parasites.
(d) All molluscs bear shell.
Which of the statement given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Every vertebrate belongs to phylum Chordata, so (a) alone holds; not all birds fly, not all insects are parasites, and not all molluscs have a shell.

questions.text: Bryophytes differ from pteridophytes in being ______
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Bryophytes lack true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem), whereas pteridophytes are vascular; that non-vascular trait is the basic difference the stem asks for.

questions.text:
Which pesticide is used to control powdery mildew ?
(a) Bordo mixture
(b) Sulphur
(c) Endosulphon
(d) Alum
Which of the option given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Bordo mixture and sulphur are standard fungicides against powdery mildew; endosulphon is mainly an insecticide and alum is not the usual choice here.

questions.text: Who proposed the natural system of classification of plants ?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Bentham and Hooker's natural system of classification (Genera Plantarum) is the classic answer; Engler–Prantl used a phylogenetic arrangement, not the natural system label.

questions.text: The basic difference in the DNA and RNA is with respect to :

options.A: The type of sugar and the type of nitrogenous base.
options.B: The type of sugar and phosphoric acid.
options.C: Type of nitrogenous base and phosphoric acid.
options.D: Type of sugar, type of nitrogenous base and number of strands (single or double stranded).

questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. DNA has deoxyribose, commonly double-stranded, with thymine; RNA has ribose, is usually single-stranded, and carries uracil instead of thymine — sugar, base, and strand number all differ.

questions.text: Coliforms are used as indicator organisms of sewage pollution because :

options.C: They are abundant in human intestine.

questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Coliform bacteria live in large numbers in the human intestine; finding them in water signals faecal contamination — the key marks abundance in the gut as the reason, not pathogenicity alone.

questions.text: The first transposons were discovered in Zea Mays, in 1948, by ______.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Barbara McClintock discovered transposable elements (transposons) in maize (Zea mays) in 1948; Mullis, Cohen, and Boyer belong to PCR and recombinant-DNA work.

questions.text:
Ajinkya, Ramesh and Vaibhav got first, second and third rank. But not in this sequence. After asking them they replied two answers each. Out of which one is true and other is false. But not in the same sequence. Their answers are as following.
Ramesh : I got first rank. Ajinkya got second rank.
Vaibhav : I got first rank. Ramesh got second rank.
Ajinkya : I got first rank. Ramesh got third rank.
Which is not the rank of Ajinkya ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Each boy makes one true and one false claim; the consistent ranking is Vaibhav first, Ajinkya second, Ramesh third — so Ajinkya cannot be first.

questions.text:
Study given information and conclusions based on it. Select logically correct conclusion/s.
Four men are waiting at the airport. Two are doctors and the other two are businessman. Two speak Gujarati and two speak Tamil. Two are Muslims and two are Christen. No two men of the same profession are of same religion nor do they speak same language. The Tamil speaking doctor is a Christen.
Conclusions :
(I) Christen business man speaks Gujarati.
(II) Gujarati speaking doctor is Muslim.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. The Tamil-speaking doctor is Christian, so the Gujarati-speaking doctor must be Muslim; no two doctors share religion or language. Conclusion (II) follows; (I) about the Christian businessman speaking Gujarati is not forced.

questions.text:
Study given information :
Persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting on benches in the garden facing north. B is 50 m to the right of D, A is 60 m to the south of B. C is 40 m to the west of D, and E is 80 m to the north of A. Select most appropriate option that describes approximate minimum distance between C and E in metres.

options.A: It must be definitely greater than 110 m.
options.B: It must be definitely most nearest to 92 m.
options.C: It must be definitely most nearest to 91 m.
options.D: It must be definitely less than 110 m.

questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Plot the positions: C at (−40, 0) and E at (50, 20), so distance = √(90² + 20²) ≈ 92.2 m — nearest to 92 m among the choices.

questions.text: A is a daughter of B, C is a sister of A, B is a daughter of D and E is a brother of C. So what is the relation between E and D ?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option D. A and C are daughters of B; E is their brother, so E is B's son; B is D's daughter — hence E is D's grandson and D is E's grandmother.

questions.text: By subtracting 5 from a number and dividing it by 7, the answer obtained is 2. Then find the value, by subtracting 4 from the same number and dividing it by 3.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. (x − 5) ÷ 7 = 2 gives x = 19; then (19 − 4) ÷ 3 = 5 — work the first equation for x before substituting into the second.

questions.text:
A, B, C and D are working on Mark's farm. He gave in all twenty watermelons to all of them. One of them got two, another one got four, third one got six, and fourth one got eight. A got more melons than B and D got fewer melons than C. If C gets at least two more melons than D then select the statement/s that is always true.
(a) A will always get more melons than C.
(b) C will never have melons equal to that of A.
(c) It is not possible for D to get more melons than any other person working with him.
(d) B will always get fewer melons than A.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Melons are fixed at 2, 4, 6, and 8; the stem already says A gets more than B, so B always gets fewer than A. A need not beat C, and D can hold 6 while another gets 8.

questions.text:
A survey conducted among 480 students of two colleges C₁ and C₂ regarding the type of computers they use, resulted in the following data (table), with partial information. It is known that the ratio of number of students of C₁ and that of C₂ is 9 : 7.

College | Desktop | Laptop | Both | None
C₁ | — | — | — | 15
C₂ | 120 | — | 30 | —
Total | — | 195 | 70 | 40

How many students of college C₁ have at least one system?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Total 480 in ratio 9: 7 gives C₁ = 270; with 15 students in C₁ having no system, at least one system = 270 − 15 = 255.

questions.text: Among participants gathered for seminar 32 persons drink tea, 35 persons drink coffee and 22 persons drink tea and coffee. Select the number of persons gathered for seminar.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. By inclusion–exclusion: 32 + 35 − 22 = 45 persons in the seminar — some drink only tea, only coffee, or both.

questions.text:
Select logically appropriate triangular image without changing its position in the plane or flipping for completing hexagonal image having one part concealed.
[Figure: A hexagon divided into six equilateral triangles; one triangle is concealed (cross-hatched). The remaining five triangles each show three symbols at the vertices — a solid black diamond, a hollow white diamond, and a curved clockwise arrow — in a rotational pattern. Four answer choices show candidate triangles with the same three symbols arranged differently.]
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A (Option 1 in the figure). The concealed triangle must carry the same three vertex symbols — solid diamond, hollow diamond, and clockwise arrow — in the rotation that completes the hexagonal pattern; without the printed diagram, follow the official answer for scoring.

questions.text:
Choose the proper option for replacing question mark in the given number series.
4, 13, 38, __?__, 168, 289, 458
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Successive odd-square jumps: +9, +25, +49, +81 … (3², 5², 7², 9²), so 38 + 49 = 87; the next steps 87 + 81 = 168 and 168 + 121 = 289 confirm it.

questions.text: Sameer has purchased an old T.V. for ₹ 4,700 and spent ₹ 800 for its repairing. He sold it for ₹ 5,800. Find his percentage profit.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Total cost = ₹4,700 + ₹800 = ₹5,500; profit = ₹300; profit % = (300 ÷ 5500) × 100 = 5⁵⁄₁₁%.

questions.text: Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite each on either side of the road, which is 80 m wide. From a point between them on the road, the angle of elevation of the top of the poles are 60° and 30°, respectively. What is the height of the poles?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Equal poles, 80 m apart: if the point is 20 m from one base, height = 20 tan 60° = 20√3 m — the 60° and 30° angles fix the same height.

questions.text:
Find the value of x in the following sequence.
3, 7, 15, 31, x, 127, 255, 511
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Each term is double the previous plus one: 31 × 2 + 1 = 63; the chain 63 → 127 → 255 → 511 follows the same rule.

questions.text: The present ages of Swati and Priti are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 7 years they will be in the ratio 11 : 16. The present age of Priti is :
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Present ages 3x and 5x; after 7 years (3x + 7)/(5x + 7) = 11/16 gives x = 5, so Priti's present age = 5 × 5 = 25 years.

questions.text: The difference between the compound interest and simple interest for 2 years at 4% p.a. on a certain sum is ₹ 8. Find the sum.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)² = P × 0.0016; setting 8 = 0.0016P gives P = ₹5,000.

title: MPSC गट-क सेवा संयुक्त पूर्व परीक्षा 2019 (मराठी)

questions.text:
'ग्रीन पीस अॅण्ड एअर व्हिज्युअल अनॅलिसिस ऑफ पोल्यूशन' अहवालामध्ये जगातील सर्वाधिक प्रदूषित शहरे जाहीर करण्यात आली. त्यापैकी 30 सर्वाधिक प्रदूषित शहरांमध्ये 22 शहरे भारतातील आहेत. खालील शहरे वायु प्रदूषणाच्या क्रमवारीत चढत्या क्रमाने लावा.
(a) दिल्ली (b) नोएडा (c) गुरूग्राम (d) गाझियाबाद
questions.explanation: परीक्षकाने पर्याय B चिन्हांकित केला. Greenpeace आणि AirVisual च्या 2018 World Air Quality Report नुसार Gurugram, Ghaziabad, Noida, Delhi या चारही शहरे जगातील सर्वाधिक प्रदूषित शहरांमध्ये होती — अधिकृत उत्तर नुसार वाढत्या rank क्रमाने Gurugram → Ghaziabad → Noida → Delhi. प्रदूषण ranking दरवर्षी बदलते; 2018 अहवालातील क्रम MPSC ने अपेक्षित केला.

questions.text: कझाखस्तानच्या पहिल्या राष्ट्रपतीच्या सन्मानार्थ, कझाखस्तानची पूर्व राजधानी 'अस्ताना' चे नाव राष्ट्रपतीच्या नावाने बदलण्यात आली आहे. नव्या राजधानीचे नाव _______ आहे.
questions.explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय A. March 2019 मध्ये Kazakhstan ने Astana हे नाव बदलून Nursultan ठेवले — पहिल्या राष्ट्राध्यक्ष Nursultan Nazarbayev यांच्या सन्मानार्थ. Tokayev नंतर राष्ट्राध्यक्ष; Nazarbayev हे व्यक्तीचे नाव, नवीन राजधानीचे नाव नाही.

questions.text:
योग्य कथने ओळखा : (पद्म पुरस्कार, 2019)
(a) तिजनबाई आणि अनिल कुमार नाईक यांना पद्म विभूषण पुरस्काराने सन्मानित करण्यात आले.
(b) धरमपाल गुलटी आणि बचेंद्री पाल यांना पद्म भूषण पुरस्काराने सन्मानित करण्यात आले.
(c) एस. थिमक्का आणि देवेंद्र स्वरूप यांना पद्म भूषण पुरस्काराने सन्मानित करण्यात आले.
(d) मनोज वाजपेयी आणि सुदाम काटे यांना पद्मश्री पुरस्काराने सन्मानित करण्यात आले.
questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय C येतो.
