questions.text: Which Indian Economist has been appointed on the UN high level advisory board for socio-economic challenges in post Covid-19 World?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Economist Jayati Ghosh was appointed to the UN Secretary-General's High-Level Advisory Board on Economic and Social Affairs for post-Covid recovery. Amartya Sen and Raghuram Rajan are prominent Indian economists but were not named to this specific board; Arundhati Roy is a novelist.

questions.text: PSA Oxygen plants were sanctioned for installation in public health facilities. What is the expansion of PSA?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. PSA stands for Pressure Swing Adsorption, the technology behind on-site medical oxygen plants that separate oxygen from air under pressure. The other expansions mix plausible-sounding words but are not the standard term used when government sanctioned PSA plants for hospitals.

questions.text: Who among the following has developed World's First bulletproof helmet against AK-47 Bullet?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. DRDO scientist Anoop Mishra developed the world's first bulletproof helmet tested to stop an AK-47 round at close range. Bipin Rawat was Army Chief; Vedprakash Malik and Ranjan Mathai held top military and diplomatic posts but did not design this helmet.

questions.text: 'My Pad My Right' project, an initiative of NABARD, has been launched in which state?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. NABARD's 'My Pad My Right' menstrual-hygiene project was launched in Tripura to improve access to sanitary products for rural women and girls. Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh run other NABARD-backed rural schemes but not this specific pad-rights initiative in 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following countries has changed a word in its National Anthem to honour indigenous people?
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Australia changed one word in its national anthem — from 'young' to 'one' — to honour Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the country's first nations. Italy, France, and Spain did not make a comparable anthem edit around this period.

questions.text: Which country has been certified as Malaria-free by the World Health Organisation on June 30, 2021?
questions.explanation: Go with option D. On 30 June 2021 the WHO certified China as malaria-free after a seventy-year elimination drive. Bangladesh and India still carry malaria burden; Canada has long been free but was not the country certified on that specific June 2021 date.

questions.text: Which country has launched the first Arctic-monitoring Satellite 'Arktika-M'?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Russia launched the Arktika-M satellite in 2021 to monitor weather, climate, and the Arctic environment from a highly elliptical orbit. Japan, China, and Germany operate polar and weather satellites but Arktika-M is a Russian programme.

questions.text: Which state Government has declared a fish named 'Copper Mahseer' as the 'State Fish'?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Sikkim declared Copper Mahseer (Neolissochilus hexagonolepis) as its state fish to spotlight Himalayan freshwater biodiversity. Assam, Odisha, and Manipur have their own state symbols but not this fish designation.

questions.text: What is the name of a trilateral program by the UK, the US and Australia to take up security challenges in the Indo-Pacific?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. AUKUS is the September 2021 security pact among Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States focused on the Indo-Pacific, including the nuclear-submarine deal. INDPAC, UUSA, and 'None of above' are distractors.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book titled 'The Battle of Rezang La'?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Kulpreet Yadav authored 'The Battle of Rezang La', recounting the 1962 last stand of 13 Kumaon at Rezang La. Santosh Yadav is a mountaineer; Neha Singh and Vijay Dahiya are writers but not under this title on the 1962 battle.

questions.text: Which of the following country has appointed Anita Anand of Indian origin as its new Defence Minister?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Anita Anand, of Indian origin, became Canada's Defence Minister in October 2021. England, America, and France have had diverse cabinets but not this specific Indian-origin defence appointment at that time.

questions.text: Asia's longest high-speed track for automobiles has been developed at _______.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. NATRAX at Pithampur near Indore hosts Asia's longest high-speed track for automobile testing — about 11.3 km. Pune, Mumbai, and Chennai have automotive hubs but not this record track facility.

questions.text: Which state has launched a portal named ILGMS?
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Kerala's ILGMS — Integrated Local Governance Management System — is a portal for panchayat-level governance and citizen services. Assam, Odisha, and Nagaland run e-governance portals but ILGMS is Kerala's branded platform.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the director of the Zoological Survey of India?
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Dhriti Banerjee became the first woman Director of the Zoological Survey of India in August 2021. Ashok Singh, Sneha Aggarwal, and Drishti Dhamija are not the ZSI director named in that landmark appointment.

questions.text: Emma Mckeon is the first female swimmer to win seven medals at Single Olympic games, she is a citizen of which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Pick option B. Emma McKeon of Australia won seven swimming medals at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics — the first female swimmer to reach that single-Games tally. USA, Germany, and England produced strong swimmers but not this seven-medal record in Tokyo.

questions.text: Which of the following contains the wording "To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India"?

options.B: Directive principles of the state policy

questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Article 51-A(c) of the Fundamental Duties reads: 'To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.' The Preamble speaks of unity and integrity in broad terms; Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights do not carry this exact duty wording.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding an Advocate General of the state:
(a) He must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
(b) He enjoys all the privileges and immunities that are available to a judge of a High Court.
(c) He receives remuneration that is available to a judge of a High Court.
(d) He holds office for a period of five years or up to the age of 62 years.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Only statement (a) holds: the Advocate General must be qualified to be appointed a High Court judge. He does not enjoy all judicial privileges, does not draw a judge's salary, and holds office during the Governor's pleasure — not for a fixed five-year or 62-year term.

questions.text: Which of the following committees recommended the direct election of Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. The P.B. Patil Committee recommended direct election of the Sarpanch in Maharashtra's Panchayati Raj setup. Baburao Kale, Bongirwar, and Vasantrao Naik committees dealt with other local-governance reforms — useful to separate when MPSC mixes committee names.

questions.text: Under which of the following articles, a High Court can issue writs?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other purposes within their territorial jurisdiction. Articles 220–221 cover High Court judges' conditions of service; Article 213 is the Governor's ordinance power.

questions.text:
Which statement is not correct regarding 'Gram Sabha'?
(1) It is a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village comprised within the area of the panchayat level.
(2) It is a village assembly consisting of all the registered voters in the area of the Panchayat.
(3) Its powers have been determined by the Central Government.
(4) Its powers and functions at village level are like State Legislature at the state level.
questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The printed key pointed to statement (1) as incorrect, but (1) and (2) both describe registered voters in the panchayat area, while (3) wrongly assigns Gram Sabha powers to the Central Government instead of the State Legislature — MPSC withdrew the item rather than score one letter.

questions.text: Which of the following articles deals with the grants in aid by the Union Government to the states?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Article 275 provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to certain states — including sums on the recommendation of the Finance Commission and special grants under the Constitution. Article 270 deals with tax distribution; 280 establishes the Finance Commission; 265 bars unauthorised taxation.

questions.text: Which of the following statement regarding the Glasgow Conference is not true?

options.A: Glasgow conference was based on climate change.
options.B: All the participating countries agreed on less Carbon Emission.
options.C: India will reduce Carbon Emission upto zero till 2070.
options.D: India will reduce Carbon Emission upto zero till 2030.

questions.explanation: The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The official option A marks 'Glasgow conference was based on climate change' as not true, yet COP26 at Glasgow was explicitly a climate summit; statement D (India net-zero by 2030) is the plainly false claim because India pledged 2070 — MPSC withdrew the item.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement is not true?
(1) The date of implementation of Indian Constitution is November 26, 1949.
(2) 'Secular' word was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
(3) The 42nd Constitutional Amendment was done in 1976.
(4) The ideals of Social, Economic and Political justice has been drawn from the Russian (USSR) Constitution.
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Statement (1) is false: 26 November 1949 is when the Constitution was adopted, not when it came into force — that date is 26 January 1950. Statements (2), (3), and (4) are standard textbook points on the 42nd Amendment and the Russian Constitution's influence on the justice ideals.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Under article 3, Parliament can create a new state out of a state by separating territory.
(b) Parliament can alter boundaries and names of states.
(c) The Bill Seeking creation of new state requires prior recommendation of President.
(d) It is obligatory to accept the advice or opinion of the state assembly concerned, on such bill.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Go with option C. Under Article 3, Parliament may create a new state by separating territory, alter boundaries and names, and such a bill needs the President's prior recommendation. Statement (d) is incorrect because the state assembly's view must be ascertained and considered — it is not obligatory for Parliament to accept it.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) The total number of ministers, excluding the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a state shall not exceed 15 percent of the total strength of legislative assembly of that state.
(b) The total number of ministers, excluding the Chief Minister, in a state shall not be less than 12.
questions.explanation: Pick option D. Both statements are false. The 91st Amendment caps the Council of Ministers at 15% of the assembly strength including the Chief Minister — not excluding the CM. There is no constitutional rule that a state must have at least twelve ministers; that minimum was discussed but never enacted.

questions.text:
Who from the following persons did not join the Indian National Congress, but gave financial and other help to the freedom movement?
(a) Jamnalal Bajaj
(b) Vadilal Lallubhai Mehta
(c) G.D. Birla
(d) Lala Shankarlal
(e) Walchand Hirachand
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. G.D. Birla and Walchand Hirachand bankrolled the nationalist cause without ever joining the Congress — industrial patrons who stayed outside party membership. Jamnalal Bajaj and Lala Shankarlal were active Congressmen, and Vadilal Lallubhai Mehta is counted among the party fold, so they drop out of the 'non-member donor' pair.

questions.text: Bhagwantrao, the king of _______ was hanged on 20th May 1857 because the British suspected that he had helped the mutineers.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Bhagwantrao, Raja of Peth in the Nashik belt, was hanged on 20 May 1857 after the British suspected him of aiding the mutineers. Nandur-Shingote, Harsul, and Dindori were other princely theatres of 1857 but not this specific name-and-date pairing.

questions.text: 16 October 1905 is recognized as:
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. 16 October 1905 is the day Curzon's Partition of Bengal took effect — nationalists marked it as a Day of Mourning. It is not Independence, Republic, or Workers' Day; the date sits on the Bengal divide calendar.

questions.text: Who started Air Transport in India in 1911 A.D.?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. French pilot George Light flew the first commercial airmail leg — Allahabad to Naini — in 1911, marking the birth of civil aviation in India. Jones, Stuart, and Derby are near-miss colonial aviator names in the distractor set.

questions.text: Which of the following was the objective of Prarthana Sabha?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Atmaram Pandurang's Prarthana Samaj aimed chiefly at the moral and religious reform of society — prayer-house reformism at its core. Opposing caste and stirring national awareness were allied goals; 'purification movement' fits Arya Samaj better than Prarthana Sabha.

questions.text: In which district in Maharashtra the underground movement had started first?
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. The underground Quit India resistance in Maharashtra is traced earliest to Satara district — Patri Sarkar and parallel-government folklore anchor that claim. Chandrapur, Jalgaon, and Thane had later or weaker underground phases in comparative Maharashtra narratives.

questions.text: Which Princely state got recognized as the first one to make primary education compulsory?
questions.explanation: Go with option A. Baroda under Sayajirao Gaekwad pioneered compulsory primary education among princely states — an 1890s decree ahead of wider British-India moves. Aund-Satara, Kolhapur-Baroda combos, and Junagad-Hyderabad lag Baroda's first-mover tag.

questions.text: Who among the following called Lokmanya Tilak as a 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
questions.explanation: Pick option B. Imperial journalist Sir Valentine Chirol of The Times dubbed Lokmanya Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest' after the 1908 trials. Allan Octavian Hume founded the Congress; Aurobindo Ghosh and Agarkar are reformers but not the source of that label.

questions.text: When was National Educational Council established?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. The National Educational Council (Rashtriya Shikshan Parishad) was established on 15 August 1906 — Tilak-era national education response to Curzon's policies. The 1947 and 1950 dates confuse Independence and Republic with this colonial council's founding.

questions.text: Which Law, made 'Governor General' as Viceroy?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The Government of India Act of 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown and renamed the Governor General as Viceroy — post-1857 reorganisation. The 1861 and 1919 Acts came later; 1957 is a typo distractor.

questions.text: Who established the 'Akhil Bharatiya Harijan Sangh'?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. Mahatma Gandhi founded the Akhil Bharatiya Harijan Sangh in 1932 to organise anti-untouchability work — a post-Poona Pact platform. Ambedkar led separate Dalit organisations; Naoroji and Gokhale belong to an earlier reform phase.

questions.text:
Match the following:
(a) Madanlal Dhingra - (i) Establishment of Mitra-Mela
(b) Anant Laxman Kanhere - (ii) Attack on John Balmfield Fuller
(c) Vinayak Damodar Sawarkar - (iii) Murder of Jackson, Collector of Nashik
(d) Hemchandra Das - (iv) Murder of Curzon Wyllie
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Pair each revolutionary with the act: Madanlal Dhingra — Curzon Wyllie murder (iv); Anant Laxman Kanhere — Jackson, Nashik collector (iii); Savarkar — Mitra-Mela (i); Hemchandra Das — Fuller attack (ii). Swapping Wyllie with Jackson scrambles the martyr map.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true about Jaganath Shankar Seth?
(a) Architect of Mumbai
(b) First Fellow of Mumbai University
(c) Established New English School
(d) First Member of Bombay Province Legislature
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Jagannath Shankar Seth — called 'Architect of Mumbai' — was the first Fellow of Bombay University and an early member of the Bombay Province Legislature; New English School credit goes to others. Key bundles (a), (b), and (d), not (c).

questions.text: Who is known as the first revolutionary?
questions.explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Vasudev Balvant Phadke — leader of the 1879 Ramoshi revolt — is termed India's first revolutionary in Maharashtra school history. Savarkar, Rammohan Roy, and Shyamji Krishna Varma belong to later revolutionary or reform phases.

questions.text:
Who started the self-reliant scheme called 'Earn and Learn' for the education of poor children?
(a) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedker and Mahatma Phule
(b) Mahatma Phule
(c) Maharshi Shinde and Agarkar
(d) Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil
questions.explanation: Go with option D. Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil alone started the Earn-and-Learn scheme at Rayat Shikshan Sanstha — work-study for poor students. Phule, Ambedkar, and Agarkar-Shinde pairs pursued different education reforms without Patil's branded scheme.

questions.text: What is sex ratio of 0 to 6 age group population in Maharashtra as per the census 2011?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Census 2011 placed Maharashtra's child sex ratio (0–6 age group) at 894 females per 1000 males — the official census figure. 864, 854, and 898 are close distractors; lock the 894 statistic for this demographic MCQ.

questions.text: Which is the second tallest mountain peak in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Kalsubai tops Maharashtra; Salher (~1567 m) in Nashik district holds second place among the peaks listed. Torna and Ghodav are lower Sahyadri forts and hills — Salher takes the silver rank.

questions.text: According to the 2011 census, which of the following district has highest female literacy?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Amravati district led female literacy among the four listed in Census 2011 — Vidarbha's relatively higher female literacy belt. Beed, Jalna, and Nandurbar show lower female literacy in this comparison set.

questions.text: Which is the first hydropower station in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Khopoli (Tata Hydro Electric scheme on the Ulhas) was Maharashtra's first major hydropower station — operational from the 1920s. Koyna and Radhanagari came later; Veer is a smaller project name distractor.

questions.text: Which industrial region of India is known as 'Ruhr of India'?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option D. The Chota Nagpur Plateau — rich in coal and iron ore — is called the 'Ruhr of India' for its heavy-industry density. Kolkata-Hooghly, Ahmedabad-Vadodara, and Madurai-Coimbatore-Bengaluru are other regions without that nickname.

questions.text:
Match the pair:
District → Project
(a) Satara → (i) Natuwadi
(b) Amaravati → (ii) Savali
(c) Hingoli → (iii) Aandhali
(d) Ratnagiri → (iv) Shahanur
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Minor-irrigation match Per the official answer: Satara–Aandhali (iii), Amravati–Shahanur (iv), Hingoli–Savali (ii), Ratnagiri–Natuwadi (i). One wrong district–project link collapses the whole grid — match from the paper's list.

questions.text:
Match the pair:
Sanctuary → Place
(a) Tansa → (i) Jalgaon
(b) Yawal → (ii) Thane
(c) Maldhok → (iii) Solapur
(d) Nagzira → (iv) Gondiya
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Sanctuary–district pairing: Tansa–Thane (ii), Yawal–Jalgaon (i), Maldhok–Solapur (iii), Nagzira–Gondia (iv). Tansa sits in the Thane-Palghar belt and Yawal in Jalgaon — do not swap those two.

questions.text: As per census 2011, which of the following districts has high population?
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Among Aurangabad, Jalgaon, Nanded, and Yavatmal, Jalgaon had the highest population in Census 2011 — large north Maharashtra demography. Aurangabad and Nanded are big districts but Jalgaon tops this comparison quartet.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct descending order of the places in Maharashtra according to annual rainfall?
questions.explanation: Pick option B. Descending annual rainfall among these hill stations: Amboli (highest, Konkan catch), then Mahabaleshwar, Matheran, and Lonavala last — coastal Ghats beat leeward interior stations. Lonavala sits in the lighter-rain shadow of the heavy belt.

questions.text: What are the types of rural settlements in Bundelkhand region?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Bundelkhand's rocky, dissected plateau favours dispersed or isolated farm hamlets — not nucleated circular or compact villages. Semi-compact appears in fertile plains; dispersion is the textbook settlement type for this region.

questions.text: Protected area of Melghat Tiger Project has been declared as a _______ national park.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Within the Melghat Tiger Project in Amravati district, the core protected block is Gugamal National Park — that is the named national park inside the reserve. Sanjay Gandhi, Chandoli, and Priyadarshini Indira Gandhi are separate parks elsewhere in Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which dam and its reservoir is known as Wilson dam and Aurthar Lake respectively?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Wilson Dam at Bhandardara on the Pravara river impounds the reservoir popularly called Arthur Lake (the paper spells it Aurthar). Upper and Lower Wardha dams sit on the Wardha, and Ujjani is on the Bhima — neither carries the Wilson–Arthur pairing.

questions.text:
What are the causes of soil erosion in India?
(a) Deforestation
(b) Destruction of grasslands
(c) Shifting agriculture
(d) Wrong methods of cultivation
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Deforestation strips protective cover, destruction of grasslands exposes topsoil, shifting (jhum) cultivation clears slopes repeatedly, and poor ploughing or overgrazing speed runoff — all four are textbook drivers of soil erosion in India, not just one cause.

questions.text: Assam has the largest reservoirs of _______ in India.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Assam's Brahmaputra valley and adjoining tracts hold the country's largest onshore petroleum reserves — Digboi, Naharkatiya, and Moran are the classic names. Iron ore and coal dominate other states; Assam is the oil belt.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are incorrect?
(a) Chikhaldara is a hill station and located in Satpuda mountain range.
(b) Gavilgad and Melghat mountains are found in southern part of Maharashtra state.
(c) Balaghat mountains are found to the north of Shambhu Mahadev mountain ranges.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Chikhaldara is a Satpuda hill station and statement (a) holds; Balaghat lies north of the Shambhu Mahadev stretch as in (c). Only statement (b) is incorrect — Gavilgad and Melghat ranges sit in northern Vidarbha, not the southern part of Maharashtra.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Absolute poverty can be eradicated.
(b) Relative poverty is based on comparison of lower income group with higher income group.
(c) Poverty is not responsible for degradation of environment.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Absolute poverty can in principle be wiped out once everyone clears a fixed minimum standard, and relative poverty is measured by comparing lower-income groups with richer ones. Statement (c) is wrong — poverty often pushes over-exploitation of forests and commons, harming the environment.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are incorrect?
(a) Currency notes in circulation are issued by the Government of India.
(b) Narrow money or M1 includes currency with the public.
questions.explanation: Go with option A. Currency notes (except the one-rupee note) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India, not directly by the Government of India — so statement (a) is incorrect. Narrow money M1 does include currency held by the public, making (b) correct.

questions.text:
The implementation of SGSY is done by:
(a) Commercial Bank
(b) Regional Rural Bank
(c) Co-operative Bank
(d) Foreign Bank
questions.explanation: Pick option C. Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) credit was routed through commercial banks, regional rural banks, and co-operative banks at the field level — the rural banking network, not foreign banks.

questions.text: What kind of unemployment arises due to the use of Sophisticated Technology?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. When firms adopt sophisticated labour-saving technology, fewer workers are needed for the same output — that displacement is called technical unemployment. Cyclical ties to recessions, seasonal to harvest cycles, and disguised to surplus farm labour.

questions.text:
Development Financial Institutions were established to _______.
(a) provide short term funds
(b) develop industry, agriculture and other key sectors
(c) regulate the money market
(d) regulate the capital market
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Development Financial Institutions (IDBI, NABARD, NHB, etc.) were set up to channel long-term funds into industry, agriculture, and other priority sectors — not to regulate money or capital markets, and not for short-term working capital alone.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) NABARD offers loans for agricultural sector development.
(b) NABARD provides loans to rural business.
(c) NABARD makes financial loans for the urban industries.
(d) NABARD provides financial support for urban development.
Which of the above statement/s are correct?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option B. NABARD refinances and supports agricultural development and rural non-farm enterprise — both (a) and (b) fit its mandate. Urban industry finance and urban development (c) and (d) fall outside NABARD's core rural-agricultural brief.

questions.text: Which of the following concept is related to the concept of "National Income"?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. National income is measured over a period — a flow variable like wages or exports — not a stock snapshot at one date. Micro is a level of analysis, not the flow-versus-stock distinction.

questions.text: What is a balance budget?

options.A: Public revenue is less than public expenditure.
options.B: Public revenue is higher than public expenditure.
options.C: Public revenue and public expenditure are the same.

questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. A balanced budget means total public revenue equals total public expenditure in that year — neither a deficit nor a surplus. Less revenue than spending is deficit; more revenue than spending is surplus.

questions.text:
Which are the founder countries of BRICS BANK?
(a) Brazil, Russia, India
(b) China, South Africa
(c) Japan, Germany, Switzerland
(d) Belgium, South Corea
questions.explanation: On this one, option B is correct. The New Development Bank (BRICS Bank) was founded by the five BRICS members — Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa — matching groups (a) and (b). Japan, Germany, Belgium, and South Korea are not founders.

questions.text:
Demographic transition is a result of _______.
(a) Changes in mortality
(b) Changes in fertility
(c) Changes in income distribution
(d) Urbanization
questions.explanation: Go with option B. Demographic transition tracks how death rates and birth rates fall as societies modernise — mortality and fertility changes drive the shift from high to low growth. Income distribution alone is not the standard textbook trigger; urbanisation often accompanies the transition but the core pair is (a) and (b).

questions.text: Under which scheme free gas connections are given to poor women?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana gives free LPG connections to women from BPL households — the gas-connection scheme. Saubhagya is electricity, Jeevan Jyoti is life insurance, and Jan-Dhan is bank accounts.

questions.text: Who receives income from Income Tax?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Income tax is levied and collected by the Union (Central) Government under the Income Tax Act — it is not assigned to states, local bodies, or UTs as their own tax head.

questions.text: Which of the following schemes has not been introduced for reducing poverty in India?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Employment Guarantee, Jawahar Rozgar Yojana, and Swarnajayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana were all anti-poverty employment programmes. A Cultural Development Programme promotes arts and heritage — it is not a poverty-reduction scheme.

questions.text: In which sector, India is suffering more due to "WTO"?
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Under WTO, TRIPs (Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights) hit India hardest — patent rules on medicines, seeds, and technology raised costs for generics and agriculture. Cultural, tourism, and political sectors are not the classic TRIPs battleground.

questions.text: Which of the following taxes is not the indirect tax in Indian Economy?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Corporation tax is paid directly by companies on profits — a direct tax. Sales tax, excise duty, and customs duties are passed on through prices and are indirect taxes.

questions.text: Who discovered radioactivity?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Henri Becquerel discovered natural radioactivity in 1896 while studying uranium salts — Marie Curie later isolated radium, Rutherford mapped the nucleus, and Einstein gave E = mc².

questions.text: _______ are commonly used as rear view mirrors in vehicles.
questions.explanation: On this one, option D is correct. Convex mirrors curve outward and give a wider field of view, so drivers see more of the road behind despite a smaller image — standard fit for rear-view mirrors. Plane mirrors show true size but too narrow; concave mirrors can invert and distort at close range.

questions.text: Energy equivalent of mass 1 u is _______.
questions.explanation: Go with option C. From Einstein's E = mc², one atomic mass unit (1 u) of mass converts to about 931 MeV of energy — the figure every nuclear-physics table lists. 911, 921, and 941 MeV are near-miss distractors.

questions.text: Which of the following metal cannot be extracted from aqueous solution of its salt?
questions.explanation: Pick option A. Potassium sits very high in the reactivity series — it reacts violently with water, so it cannot be won by simple displacement from an aqueous salt solution; it needs electrolysis of the molten salt. Copper, silver, and gold are less reactive and can be extracted electrolytically from aqueous solutions.

questions.text: _______ is an important ore of aluminium.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B matches the key. Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is tied to aluminium extraction in the Hall–Héroult process as a flux, though bauxite is the actual ore — if the stem reads differently on the original paper, trust the key's Cryolite label.

questions.text: The set of the elements belonging to S-block is _______.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. S-block elements occupy groups 1 and 2 — Na, Ca, Ba and Ra all sit there; Ta is d-block and Be–Re–Ge–Se mix different blocks.

questions.text: Which of the following set of terms is best applicable to Obelia?

options.D: Marine, Sedentary, Colonial, Polymorphic with true alternation of generation

questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Obelia is a marine, sedentary, colonial hydrozoan that is polymorphic and shows true alternation of generations between polyp and medusa stages.

questions.text: The number of legs found in Peripatus is _______.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. Peripatus (Onychophora) bears 14–43 pairs of stubby, unjointed legs along its body — that range is the standard textbook figure.

questions.text: Generic name of cockroach 'Periplaneta' was assigned by:
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. The generic name Periplaneta for the cockroach was established by Burmeister in 1838; Linnaeus used Blatta for related forms.

questions.text: Which of the followings are known as Amphibians of plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Bryophytes live on land but need water for sexual reproduction, so they are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom — not pteridophytes or seed plants.

questions.text: Insecticide poison the insect pests by affecting their _______.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Most chemical insecticides are neurotoxins — they block nerve signal transmission in pests, which stops feeding and movement quickly.

questions.text:
Which of the following is correct statement/statements regarding inorganic nutrients in plants?
(a) N, S and Fe are macronutrients
(b) O, Ca and Mg are Micronutrients
(c) Cu, Zn and Mn are essential elements
(d) B, Mo and Cl are non-essential elements
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. The key marks (a) and (c): N and S are macronutrients and Cu, Zn, Mn are essential micronutrients; (b) wrongly lists O, Ca, Mg as micronutrients and (d) wrongly calls B, Mo, Cl non-essential.

questions.text: West Nile Encephalitis (WNE) is the inflammation of the _______ caused by West Nile Virus. WNE was first diagnosed in the West Nile region of _______.
questions.explanation: The right pick is option A. West Nile encephalitis is inflammation of the brain caused by West Nile virus; the disease was first identified in the West Nile district of Uganda in 1937.

questions.text: White Button Mushrooms are scientifically (Biologically) named as _______.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. The common white button mushroom is Agaricus bisporus; Pleurotus and Volvariella are oyster and paddy-straw mushrooms respectively.

questions.text: _______ hormone is released when water content of blood fluids is less than normal.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. When blood fluid volume drops, the posterior pituitary releases vasopressin (ADH), which reduces water loss in urine and helps restore fluid balance.

questions.text: If the letter group HJLN is coded as ILOR, then by the same principal what could be the correct code for the letter group DFHJ?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Each letter shifts forward by an increasing step: +1, +2, +3, +4 — so D→E, F→H, H→K, J→N gives EHKN.

questions.text:
Given below are 5 statements followed by options composed of 3 statements put together in a specific order. Choose the option that indicates logically valid argument. To be valid the 3rd statement of the composition should be the conclusion based on preceding 2 statements.
(a) Modern industry is research driven.
(b) 'Impro' is a modern industry.
(c) 'Impro' is research driven.
(d) 'Impro' may be research driven.
(e) Research driven industry is modern.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. The official key lists (b), (c), (e) as the valid chain; follow that sequence for scoring even though textbook syllogism practice often prefers (a), (b), (c).

questions.text:
Examine the following facts:
(a) Anu is heavier than Bano.
(b) Cynthia is taller than Dina.
(c) Bano is of same height as Dina but heavier than her.
(d) Dina is taller than Anu.
Select the correct conclusion based on above facts.

options.A: Cynthia is the heaviest and Anu is shortest of all.
options.B: Anu is definitely heaviest and shortest among all.
options.C: Cynthia is heaviest but it is impossible to conclude who is tallest of all.
options.D: It is impossible to draw conclusion about who is heaviest but Anu is definitely shortest among all.

questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. Anu is heavier than Bano and Dina is taller than Anu, so Anu is definitely the shortest; no facts compare Cynthia's weight with the others, so the heaviest person cannot be fixed.

questions.text:
Total number of books that students A, B, C and D have is thirty. One of them has three books, another one is having six, third one is having nine and fourth one is having twelve books. B is having fewer books than C and D is having more books than A. If C has fewer books than D, then select the statement/s that/those is/are not necessarily true.
(a) A and B together must have at least 12 books.
(b) D and A together must have at least 15 books.
(c) C and D together must have at least 18 books.
(d) C and B together must have at least 9 books.
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option D. With books 3, 6, 9 and 12 and the ordering B < C < D and D > A, statement (a) can be incorrect — e.g. A=3 and B=6 give only 9 together — while (b), (c) and (d) hold under every valid assignment.

questions.text:
The following is the information of Area and Population of States.
State A: Area 80,000 sq.km, Population 16 lakh
State B: Area 50,000 sq.km, Population 10 lakh
State C: Area 10,000 sq.km, Population 4 lakh
State D: Area 5,000 sq.km, Population 3 lakh
Which is the most thickly populated State?
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Population density = population ÷ area: D gives 3 lakh ÷ 5,000 sq km = 60 per sq km, ahead of C (40), A and B (both 20).

questions.text:
10 workers working with same speed were deployed to construct a structure. 2 workers left on the 2nd day, another 2 left on the 3rd day and this went on till the work is completed. As a result 2 more days were needed to complete the work.
Select the number of days that were needed if 10 workers worked for all days.
questions.explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Total work equals 10 × n worker-days; with two workers leaving each day from day 2, a 5-day run (10+8+6+4+2 = 30) matches n = 3 — so 10 workers alone would finish in 3 days.

questions.text: The price of sugar is increased by 60%. How much percent a householder should reduce the consumption of sugar so as not to increase the expenditure?
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. If price rises 60%, keep expenditure fixed by consuming 100/160 = 5/8 of the original amount — a cut of 3/8, i.e. 37½%.

questions.text: Persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting on benches in the garden facing north. B is 40 m to the right of D, A is 60 m to the south of B. C is 50 m to the west of D, and E is 70 m to the north of A. Select most appropriate option that describes approximate minimum distance between C and E in metres.

options.A: It must be definitely greater than 90 m.
options.B: It must be definitely greater than 91 m but less than 92 m.
options.C: It must be definitely greater than 90 m but is less than 91 m.
options.D: It must be definitely less than 91 m.

questions.explanation: The right pick is option C. Plotting the positions gives C at (−50, 0) and E at (40, 10), so distance = √(90² + 10²) ≈ 90.55 m — greater than 90 m but under 91 m.

The official answer key cancelled this question — treat it for practice only. The official option was (1) 24–21, but the odd-one-out pattern among the four pairs is disputed; MPSC withdrew the item rather than score one letter.

questions.text:
Consider the following order of a string of pebbles of three colours, Green (G), Blue (B) and Red (R):
X = GGBRBRRBBR
Y = GBRRBRBBRG
Z = RBBRGGBRBR
Which two of them gives us identical necklaces prepared by just making the first and last pebbles of the string adjacent?

options.D: No one of them are identical

questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Treating each string as a circular necklace, X (GGBRBRRBBR) and Z (RBBRGGBRBR) match by rotation — they are the same ring of pebbles; Y gives a different cycle.

questions.text: The denominator of a fraction is greater than the numerator by 5. If 8 is added to the numerator and 1 is subtracted from the denominator, the value of the fraction obtained is 15/11. The original fraction is _______.
questions.explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Let the numerator be n and denominator n+5; (n+8)/(n+4) = 15/11 gives n = 7, so the original fraction is 7/12.

questions.text: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 50 years. Four years ago, father's age was six times as that of his son. What are the present ages of the father and son respectively?
questions.explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Present ages sum to 50; four years ago the father was six times the son's age — solving F + S = 50 and F − 4 = 6(S − 4) gives 40 years and 10 years.

questions.text: In a school, the ratio of girls to boys is 4 : 5. If there are 76 girls find the number of boys.
questions.explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Girls: boys = 4: 5 with 76 girls means one part = 76 ÷ 4 = 19; boys = 5 × 19 = 95.

questions.text: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 2 : 5. If first train runs 350 km in 5 hours, then the difference between speeds (in km/h) of both the trains is:
questions.explanation: The right pick is option D. The first train's speed is 350 ÷ 5 = 70 km/h; with a 2: 5 ratio the second runs at 175 km/h — difference 175 − 70 = 105 km/h.

questions.text: In an examination, 35% of the students passed and 455 students failed. How many students appeared for the examination?
questions.explanation: The verified answer here is option B. If 35% passed, 65% failed and 65% of total = 455, so total students = 455 ÷ 0.65 = 700.

title: MPSC गट-क सेवा संयुक्त पूर्व परीक्षा 2021 (मराठी)

questions.text: कोविड-19 नंतरच्या जगातील सामाजिक-आर्थिक आव्हानांसंदर्भात संयुक्त राष्ट्र उच्च स्तरीय सल्लागार मंडळावर कोणत्या भारतीय अर्थतज्ञाची निवड करण्यात आली आहे?
questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय C येतो. अर्थशास्त्रज्ञ Jayati Ghosh यांना Covid-19 नंतर socioeconomic challenges साठी UN Secretary-General च्या High-Level Advisory Board वर नियुक्त केले. Amartya Sen, Raghuram Rajan नामवंत अर्थशास्त्रज्ञ, पण या विशिष्ट board वर नाहीत; Arundhati Roy साहित्यिक.

questions.text: सार्वजनिक आरोग्य सुविधांमध्ये पी.एस.ए. ऑक्सिजन प्लांट्स बसविण्यास मंजुरी देण्यात आली. पी.एस.ए. (PSA) चा विस्तार काय आहे?
questions.explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय A. PSA म्हणजे Pressure Swing Adsorption — दाबातून हवेतून oxygen वेगळा करणारी तंत्रज्ञान, ज्यावर सरकारने रुग्णालयांसाठी oxygen plants मंजूर केली. इतर expansion वाजवी वाटतात, पण हा standard संक्षिप्त नाव नाही.

questions.text: ए.के.-47 बुलेटच्या विरोधी जगातील पहिले बुलेटप्रुफ हेल्मेट खालीलपैकी कोणी विकसित केले आहे?
questions.explanation: येथे खात्रीशीर उत्तर पर्याय C. DRDO scientist Anoop Mishra यांनी AK-47 bullet थांबवणारे जगातील पहिले bulletproof helmet विकसित केले. Bipin Rawat Army Chief; Vedprakash Malik, Ranjan Mathai सैन्य/ राजनयिक पदांवर होते, हे helmet ते designing केले नाही.

questions.text: 'माय पॅड माय राईट' या नावाचा, नाबार्डचा उपक्रम कोणत्या राज्यात सुरू झाला आहे?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय C. NABARD ची 'My Pad My Right' menstrual-hygiene योजना Tripura मध्ये सुरू — ग्रामीण महिला/मुलींना sanitary products. Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh मध्ये इतर NABARD योजना, पण 2021 मध्ये ही विशिष्ट pad-rights initiative नाही.

questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणत्या देशामध्ये स्वदेशी (मूळ रहिवासी) लोकांना सन्मानित करण्यासाठी त्यांच्या राष्ट्रगीतातील एक शब्द बदलण्यात आला आहे?
questions.explanation: या प्रश्नात पर्याय C. Australia ने राष्ट्रगीतात एक शब्द बदलला — 'young' ऐवजी 'one' — Aboriginal व Torres Strait Islander लोकांना first nations म्हणून सन्मान. Italy, France, Spain ने या काळात अशा प्रकारे anthem बदल केले नाही.

questions.text:

questions.text:
ग्रामसभेच्या संदर्भात कोणते विधान योग्य नाही?

(2) पंचायतीतील सर्व नोंदणीकृत मतदारांची मिळून ग्रामसभा बनते.
(3) ग्रामसभेचे अधिकार केंद्रसरकार निर्धारित करते.
(4) त्याची ग्रामपातळीवरील अधिकार आणि कार्ये राज्यपातळीवरील राज्यविधीमंडळासारखे असतात.
questions.explanation: अधिकृत उत्तरतालिकेने हा प्रश्न रद्द केला — फक्त सरावासाठी. मुद्रित उत्तर (1) चुकीचे दर्शविले, पण (1) व (2) दोन्ही panchayat क्षेत्रातील registered voters; (3) Gram Sabha अधिकार Central Government ला देतो — State Legislature नाही — MPSC ने प्रश्न मागे घेतला.

questions.explanation: अधिकृत उत्तरतालिकेने हा प्रश्न रद्द केला — फक्त सरावासाठी. अधिकृत उत्तर A — 'Glasgow conference climate change वर' — खरे नाही म्हणते, पण COP26 Glasgow climate summit; D (India net-zero 2030) स्पष्ट चुकीचे — India ने 2070 जाहीर केले — MPSC ने प्रश्न मागे घेतला.

questions.text:
पुढीलपैकी कोणत्या व्यक्ती राष्ट्रीय महासभेत सामील झाल्या नाहीत परंतु त्यांनी स्वातंत्र्य चळवळीला आर्थिक व इतर मदत केली होती?

questions.explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय C येतो. G.D. questions.text: ________ चे राजे भगवंतराव यांना 20 मे 1857 रोजी ब्रिटीशांनी त्याने बंडखोरांना मदत केली असा आरोप ठेवून फाशी दिले.

questions.text: इ.स. 1911 मध्ये भारतात हवाई परिवहनाची सुरुवात कोणी केली?

questions.text: खालीलपैकी प्रार्थना सभेचे उद्दिष्टे कोणते होते?
questions.explanation: परीक्षकाने पर्याय A चिन्हांकित केला. Atmaram Pandurang यांच्या Prarthana Samaj चे मुख्य उद्दिष्ट society चे moral व religious reform — prayer-house reformism. Caste opposition व national awareness allied goals; 'purification movement' Arya Samaj ला अधिक जुळते Prarthana Sabha पेक्षा.

questions.text: भूमिगत चळवळ महाराष्ट्रात कोणत्या जिल्ह्यात प्रथमतः सुरु केली?
